The following is the summary of our meeting today (November 19), regarding the problem:
o Major Incident: INC4855815
o Problem: PRB2011977
o PTASK: PTASK2023826

Summary of Discussion
The meeting was a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) call to investigate an incident involving API timeouts. The initial analysis by the assigned team (CH App Services) found no errors in their logs, suggesting requests were failing before reaching their backend.
• Apigee Log Analysis:
o The Apigee team (Pranay and Mahesh) contradicted the initial findings. Their logs showed 503 Service Unavailable and timeout errors originating from the backend services, not Apigee itself.
o Target latency was extremely high (20-30 seconds), while Apigee's processing time was in milliseconds, confirming the bottleneck was with the downstream services.
• Identifying Failing Services:
o The primary failing Apigee proxy was ENT sales code V1.
o This proxy was making calls to two different backend APIs: ENT customer V1 and Bus Connect V1.
o Investigation revealed that Bus Connect V1 was operating normally, but ENT customer V1 (owned by the SAPI V4 team) was experiencing read timeouts.
• Multiple Failure Points:
o Sangeetha noted that the incident wasn't isolated to a single service. Both Connect auto and Apex auto coding flows were experiencing timeouts simultaneously, suggesting a broader issue, possibly a network glitch.
o Aparna, from the Apex auto team, confirmed her service also failed. Her logs showed that requests from her application (ASAP) never even reached the Apigee gateway. This indicated a fundamental connectivity problem between her service, hosted on Homesite AWS, and the Apigee endpoint.
• Connecting the Dots:
o Mahesh identified a common link: both failing application workflows involved services running on ECS (Elastic Container Service).
o The Connect auto flow failed when calling the SAPI V4 service, which runs on an ECS container.
o The Apex auto flow failed to connect from an ECS container on Homesite AWS.
o This strongly suggests the root of the problem lies within the ECS environment.
Conclusion
The definitive root cause could not be determined during the call due to a lack of detailed performance data and tracing in the backend services. However, the investigation strongly points to an intermittent issue within the ECS container environment, which is preventing services from communicating effectively.
Next Steps
1. Reassign RCA Task: Rene will reassign the RCA task to the Homesite DevOps team.
2. DevOps Investigation: The Homesite DevOps team is expected to investigate their ECS and CloudWatch logs from the incident timeframe to identify any anomalies that could explain the timeouts and connectivity failures.
3. Improve Monitoring: Aparna will continue with her existing task to implement better logging and tracing for the Apex auto service to ensure sufficient data is available for future troubleshooting.
4. Follow-up Meeting: Rene will schedule a follow-up meeting for the following week to discuss the findings from the Homesite DevOps team. The duplicate meeting scheduled for the same afternoon will be canceled.

Problem statement: The work queues within Homesite and perhaps other claims wk queues experiencing issues.  Claims for HS (866-621-4823) are being misrouted or disconnected.
Description: The work queues within Homesite and perhaps other claims work queues are experiencing issues.  Claims for HS (866-621-4823) are being misrouted or disconnected.
Cause notes: The Wave 5 and Wave 6 go-lives led to increased traffic on the PureConnect IVR servers, resulting in more calls being transferred to other systems. Each transfer required two call ports, causing the servers to reach their maximum port capacity. As a result, some calls were not answered and transfers occasionally failed due to unavailable call ports.
Close notes: SIP REFER (Call Putback) was enabled in the line configurations within Interaction Administrator on both IVR servers to resolve the issue, as it uses only one call port per transfer. This significantly reduced port usage and eliminated the risk of maxing out call ports. No changes were needed to MetroSwitch, as it was already configured to accept SIP REFERs.

Problem statement: Call Center and Agency Users unable to make or receive calls
Description:
• Business Impact: Agency Users are unable to make or receive calls.
•  RCA: Cause code: Hardware issue
We experienced an issue where four Genesys PureConnect ACD EC2 instances running on a dedicated host became unresponsive due to the underlying host entering a permanent failure state. These servers were all primary servers, which caused an automatic switchover to the backup servers at the same time.
Root Cause:
 • The underlying dedicated host experienced a permanent hardware failure, causing all EC2 instances on that host to become unresponsive.
 • The customer's AWS account had reached its EC2 C5 Dedicated host limit, preventing immediate allocation of a replacement host and delaying migration.
Contributing Factors:
 • Lack of automated failover or host replacement for dedicated hosts in the event of hardware failure.
 • Account limits on dedicated hosts were not proactively set to accommodate potential failure scenarios.
 • Manual intervention was required to request and apply a limit increase, resulting in additional downtime.

•  Resolution:
 • A new dedicated host was requested in AWS for the servers that were on the dedicated host that was down.
 • AWS Support escalated and processed a limit increase for EC2 C5 Dedicated hosts.
        • The customer force-stopped unresponsive instances, allocated a new host, and relaunched the instances successfully.
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No

Description:
• Business Impact: Users were unable to submit quotes for Apex Auto Quotes due to an error showing "Invalid Address" which was

• RCA: Cause Code: Vendor Issue. Cause Notes: An inadvertent tenant configuration change within Azure Front Door (AFD) triggered a widespread service disruption causing increased latencies, timeouts, and connection errors for downstream services.
• Resolution: Vendor fixed both the original control plane incompatibility, data plane bug, synchronous processing of each customer configuration, implemented additional stages in our phased configuration rollout, decoupling configuration processing, migrated critical first-party infrastructure.
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2023632. Cause Code: vendor issue. Cause Notes: What happened? Between 15:45 UTC on 29 October and 00:05 UTC on 30 October 2025, customers and Microsoft services leveraging Azure Front Door (AFD) may have experienced latencies, timeouts, and errors. Affected Azure services include, but are not limited to: App Service, Azure Active Directory B2C, Azure Communication Services, Azure Databricks, Azure Healthcare APIs, Azure Maps, Azure Portal, Azure SQL Database, Azure Virtual Desktop, Container Registry, Media Services, Microsoft Copilot for Security, Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management, Microsoft Entra ID (Mobility Management Policy Service, Identity & Access Management, and User Management UX), Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Sentinel (Threat Intelligence), and Video Indexer. Customer configuration changes to AFD remain temporarily blocked. We will notify customers once this block has been lifted. While error rates and latency are back to pre-incident levels, a small number of customers may still be seeing issues and we are still working to mitigate this long tail. Updates will be provided directly via Azure Service Health. What went wrong and why? An inadvertent tenant configuration change within Azure Front Door (AFD) triggered a widespread service disruption affecting both Microsoft services and customer applications dependent on AFD for global content delivery. The change introduced an invalid or inconsistent configuration state that caused a significant number of AFD nodes to fail to load properly, leading to increased latencies, timeouts, and connection errors for downstream services. As unhealthy nodes dropped out of the global pool, traffic distribution across healthy nodes became imbalanced, amplifying the impact and causing intermittent availability even for regions that were partially healthy. We immediately blocked all further configuration changes to prevent additional propagation of the faulty state and began deploying a ‘last known good’ configuration across the global fleet. Recovery required reloading configurations across a large number of nodes and rebalancing traffic gradually to avoid overload conditions as nodes returned to service. This deliberate, phased recovery was necessary to stabilize the system while restoring scale and ensuring no recurrence of the issue. The trigger was traced to a faulty tenant configuration deployment process. An inadvertent tenant configuration change within Azure Front Door (AFD) triggered a widespread service disruption affecting both Microsoft services and customer applications dependent on AFD for global content delivery. The change introduced an invalid or inconsistent configuration state that caused a significant number of AFD nodes to fail to load properly, leading to increased latencies, timeouts, and connection errors for downstream services. As unhealthy nodes dropped out of the global pool, traffic distribution across healthy nodes became imbalanced, amplifying the impact and causing intermittent availability even for regions that were partially healthy. We immediately blocked all further configuration changes to prevent additional propagation of the faulty state and began deploying a ‘last known good’ configuration across the global fleet. Recovery required reloading configurations across a large number of nodes and rebalancing traffic gradually to avoid overload conditions as nodes returned to service. This deliberate, phased recovery was necessary to stabilize the system while restoring scale and ensuring no recurrence of the issue. The trigger was traced to a faulty tenant configuration deployment process. Our protection mechanisms, to validate and block any erroneous deployments, failed due to a software defect which allowed the deployment to bypass safety validations. Problem statement: CFRFARM-33713 - Nonrenewal letter showing incorrect date (picking renewal term end date instead of current policy term expiration date)
Description:
Description:
The Nonrenewal Notice generated for renewal transactions is displaying the incorrect date in the letter.
Instead of showing the policy term expiration date (01/11/2026), the letter displays the renewal term's end date (01/11/2027).

Expected Behavior:
For Non-Renewing transactions, the Nonrenewal Notice should display the expiration date of the current policy term (2026-01-11) as the end of coverage, not the renewal term's period end date.

Root Cause:
PolicyCenter is correctly setting cancellationType is NonRenew when PreRenewalDirection is NonRenew.
However, SmartComm interprets this type to use the periodEndDate field instead of the cancel Date, this results in the wrong date being shown on the Nonrenewal Notice.

Reported policy: 910023270870

Steps to Recreate:
1. Open any active policy with a current term (e.g., 01/11/2025 – 01/11/2026).
2. Initiate a Renewal for the policy the renewal term will be created (e.g., 01/11/2026 – 01/11/2027).
3. In the Pre-Renewal Direction field of the policy, set the value to Non-Renew.
4. Complete the renewal process so the renewal job moves to Non-Renewing status.
5. Trigger the SendTpiCancelNotice or corresponding Nonrenewal Notice event.
6. Verify the letter generated the Nonrenewal Notice displays the date 01/11/2027.
Cause notes: Fix put in with CLPC 58.2 Release on 11/15/25. From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2023864. Cause Code: software issue. Cause Notes: Fix put in with CLPC 58.2 Release on 11/15/25.

Problem statement: CFRFARM-33672: FLR 00 13 and FLR 00 17 – Cancellation Letters not generating as per requirement
Description:
Description:
System does not function as per the defined requirements for FLR 00 13 (TPI Cancel Letter) and FLR 00 17 (UW Termination Letter).

Issue summary:
For FLR 00 13, the requirement states that Option 1 reason should be printed for all cancellation scenarios. However, the current logic restricts this behavior to cancellations where the source is Insured. As a result, for Company-initiated cancellations, the TpiCancelOption tag is not mapped, and the cancellation reason is not printed in the cancellation letter.

For FLR 00 17, the letter should trigger for Company cancellations when the product is Farmowners, but the Farmowners product is not configured in document setup under UI → Form Configuration. Hence, the Farmowners product and other required document details are missing in the FLR 00 17 form pattern, and the document is not generated.

Steps to Reproduce:

﻿﻿﻿1.Create a mid-term cancellation for a policy with source = Company
﻿﻿﻿2.Verify that the generated FLR 00 13 letter does not print the cancel reason
﻿﻿﻿3.For FLR 00 17  Farmowners product, perform a Company cancellation verify FLR 00 17 is not triggered or generated

Description:
• Business Impact: Intermittently, users of EDSP - Agency, EDSP - Customer, Guidewire Policy Center E1P, Personal Lines Policy Center, Guidewire Policy Center Rome, and Risk Appetite are unable to quote for home and renters. 
• RCA: Vendor Issue. Cause notes - Outage occurred due to a convergence of issues leading to Decision Execution, our vendor hosted environment that executes Sapiens Decision assets, going offline.
                     Few things that lead to this outage:
                    1. Our internal Sapiens Wrapper introduced retry logic where, if the connection to the vendor failed, it would retry 1 time.
                    2. We discovered that one of our internal clients retry logic is around 85 times. The combination of 1 and 2 lead to a spike in vendor calls to a point where they received 16,000 requests within 1 minute. Overwhelming the vendors servers.
                   3. Vendor server had issues with the frequency and duration of the garbage collections. This issue caused a delay in the clearing   cycle, which added to the outage occurrence.
                    4. Vendor has improvements to make on the connection between Sapiens Decision Execution and their Parameter Management  (PaM) service. This PaM service is a SQL lookup function to the database. There were failures in connections to PaM from DE, leading to  increased memory which compounded with the increase in retries. 
• Resolution: We have successfully put in place the following changes in Prod:
LOR (least outstanding request) routing to their DB servers
Oauth
Compression
Updated software versions of DM/DE/PaM
All changes combined have seen performance improvements leading to P95 of all calls being 100ms or less.
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: Yes/ CHG2172556

Problem statement: Applications encountering API and network connection failures
Description:
• Business Impact: Teams are seeing that there are multiple applications that are encountering API and/or network connection failures.
• RCA: During the AWS outage, the Bogon feed generation service was unable to communicate with the DynamoDB and also retrieve the full exclusion network list. As a result, private IP subnets were not properly excluded from the feed. 
• Resolution: Infoblox has implemented a change in design to remove the dependency on DynamoDB for the exclusion list.
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No 

.
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2023501. Cause Code: vendor issue. Cause Notes: On October 20 at 12:11 AM PDT, Amazon reported a service disruption affecting multiple AWS services in the N. Virginia region. Shortly after, at 1:00 AM PDT, the Infoblox Bogon RPZ feed (bogon.rpz.infoblox.local) started having zone data sent with private IP subnets (10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, and 172.16.0.0/12). Infoblox customers started opening support cases at 1:20AM PDT mentioning DNS resolution issues. The Infoblox Bogon RPZ feed is designed to contain reserved or non-routable IP address spaces. Infoblox maintains this feed through a feed generation service hosted in AWS, which also connects to AWS DynamoDB to exclude private IP subnets such as 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, and 172.16.0.0/12. During the AWS outage, the Bogon feed generation service was unable to communicate with the DynamoDB and also retrieve the full exclusion network list. As a result, private IP subnets were not properly excluded from the feed. Customers who had configured the Bogon RPZ feed with "Block" mode experienced DNS resolution failures for domains that were resolving to IPs within the affected private IP subnets..

Upon investigation, we discovered that certain internal networks had been inadvertently added to the feed. Further analysis determined that an internal filtering service—responsible for excluding internal networks from the feed—was disrupted during an AWS outage in the Virginia region.

Problem statement: CFRFARM-33478: CLPC: Reinstatements in the held renewal term are not sent to commissions
Description:
Description: CLPC: Reinstatements in the held renewal term are not sent to commissions

Root cause: 
Policy:  910051729763.  Policy was in held status awaiting payment.  Was cancelled and then reinstated when customer made payment.  The reinstate should have behaved like a confirmed renewal and been released to commissions, but it was not.  

It looks to be the event is still not being triggered for the eligible reinstatement. The event trigger code is executing but looks like not getting committed, hence the event is not triggering eventually.

Steps to replicate:
Create new submission and bind it.
Create a renewal for the same policy for new term.
Cancel the policy.
Reinstate the policy and check the commission message history for the reinstatement transaction.

Workaround: A script needs to be ran to trigger the event.

Organizational & Technical Complexity: Cross-Operating Company Access: A major point of confusion is the process for agents moving between supporting different AmFam operating companies (e.g., AmFam proper, Homesite, Connect). This often requires a completely separate user account and a new access request, which was not understood by Results CX leadership. Agents would lose access because they were trying to use their AFI login for a Homesite role, for example. HR-Driven Changes: The HR department would make organizational changes (e.g., changing an employee's manager or department code) without notifying the IAC team. This would break the access automation (called GroupID), causing employees to suddenly lose their permissions. The IAC team would then have to scramble to reconfigure the automation. Segregation of Duties (SoD): Some access requests were denied due to SoD policies, which are business rules outside of IAC's control that prevent users from having conflicting permissions..

So when update, insert and select queries were being executed on mfa_status table, an implicit conversion was taking place from nvarchar4000 to varchar. This wasn't an issue till the size of the table grew over 2.2M records..

It was an interaction between legitimate API usage patterns and an internal data structure that did not degrade gracefully under this edge case. An atypical workload pattern concentrated on a single cache shard in the Redis tier (data tier) created a hot partition. This pattern was recursive in nature triggering expensive lookups of high-cardinality agent state, while agents were receiving reconnect/assignment operations. This combination increased execution time for certain cache operations, which in turn slowed assignment processing. Contributing factors to root cause and extended mitigation were co-location of related interaction keys that increased hot-key effects under bursty patterns. While observability surfaced the hotspot quickly, latency attribution to the specific data pattern required deeper slow-log analysis, extending time to mitigation. The teams incorrectly suspected SQS as the culprit until continued investigation identified root cause. To mitigate the incident, events generated from the high-pressure workload were ignored, which reduced contention on the hot partition. Once this action was taken, the system processed queued events and latency returned to normal. There was an additional step taken that blocked the event type after the mitigation action to prevent recurrence. Review of this additional step is still under investigation, as it may not have been a mitigating/preventative action. However, the corrective actions listed below will prevent recurrence and improve performance of the service. Corrective Actions To prevent recurrence while code changes are in progress, the team has added telemetry that allows for Redis slow-log signals to be included in real-time observability to surface hot partition patterns sooner. Improvements to routing latency attribution will allow teams to faster identify which internal data structures and endpoints drive regional latency. Problem statement: AWS issues impacting multiple API services and applications
Description:
• Business Impact: AWS issues impacting multiple applications and services
• RCA: Because of the Typo error,  the default route was not advertised to the secondary connection as expected. This led to asymmetrical routing: the secondary connection advertised ELZ routes to Ashburn EDC, but ELZ sent its return traffic to Dallas EDC instead. 
• Resolution: CHG2171105 was completed successfully and verified by Charles Timmons that traffic was egressing the secondary Ashburn ELZ connection.
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2023108. Cause Code: people process documentation. Cause Notes: On the night of 09/17/2025, maintenance was performed on the Ashburn Equinix data center, specifically on the primary connection for AWS ELZ. AWS ELZ has two connections in Ashburn - a primary and a secondary, each on separate hardware, providing protected port connectivity. During maintenance on the primary, the secondary connection is expected to handle traffic. However, on 09/17/2025, the secondary connection did not function as designed. This was due to a typographical error in the BGP Export rule within the Ashburn internal Cloud firewall. As a result, the default route was not advertised to the secondary connection. This led to asymmetrical routing: the secondary connection advertised ELZ routes to Ashburn EDC, but ELZ sent its return traffic to Dallas EDC instead..
Close notes: CHG2171105 was completed successfully and verified by Charles Timmons that traffic was egressing the secondary Ashburn ELZ connection.

Description:
• Business Impact: Superuser Url not loading as the SSL certificate expired
• RCA: Certificate expiration notices were not assigned to the correct ServiceNow queue, resulting in the renewal incident (generated on 8/28) not being processed. The certificate expired because the established assignment process was not followed.
• Resolution: Review of certificate expiration procedures with the team to ensure everyone is on the same page with how to handle expiration notices. 
Implement procedures to track down certificates that are at T-1 day with no new certificate issued. Review the incident, contact the team, get confirmation that the certificate is going to be renewed in time. 
Manually update metadata in Keyfactor to replace the data that is missing from the Digicert import/integration. This will allow for email alerts in addition to the SNOW incident giving teams more time.

Implement job shadow / knowledge transfer with new employees in person to transition important knowledge about our environment and procedures. 
Long term: Remove humans from the certificate issuance and renewal process by implementing certificate automation. All public certificate will have a 47 day lifetime in 2027. By that date we need to be completely automated to prevent outages or constant cert renewals.

• Caused by Change: No

Cause Notes: Certificate expirations are tracked within our tool, KeyFactor, and email alerts are generated at 90, 60, 30, 15, 10, 5, and 1 day prior to expiration. If the metadata is no longer correct, it is the responsibility of the Cyber Defense team to track down the CI associated with certificate using data available in the CMDB or Confluence. Metadata was missing in the DigiCert / public facing certificates that would have added email alerts in addition to the incident which would act as a backstop to the incident for team notification. As the metadata missing included the team email address alerts were not sent to the team via email outside of SNOW. Certificate renewal is for the most part still a manual process. Cause Notes: Problem Summary Incident: Payment processing failure in commercial-quote service following code cleanup activities JIRA Reference: SBGWI-12554 Severity: High Affected Systems: Commercial Quote Service, Issue Policy API Timeline of Events Initial State: Two payment implementations existed - legacy system (unused for 2+ years) and newer 'v3' system SBGWI-12554 Development: Code cleanup initiated to remove legacy payment system and associated unused fields Code Changes Implemented: Removed feature flag controlling payment implementation selection Removed legacy payment implementation code Cleaned up unused fields from Issue Policy request body Deployment: Changes deployed to production environment Incident Triggered: Payment processing failures detected due to system not using the new payment implementation Root Cause Analysis Primary Root Cause: Incomplete feature flag removal process resulted in orphaned business logic that continued to reference the removed feature flag for payment implementation selection. Technical Details: While the feature flag and legacy payment code were successfully removed, a critical rule that used this flag to direct the system to use the 'v3' payment implementation was not identified and updated during the cleanup process Without the rule directing the system to use the new ‘v3’ payment implementation, no payment was initiated Contributing Factors Incomplete Impact Analysis: The cleanup process did not include a comprehensive scan for all dependencies on the removed feature flag Insufficient Cross-Reference Documentation: Lack of clear mapping between feature flags and rules Limited Test Coverage: Testing scenarios may not have adequately covered the payment flow path selection logic Code Archaeology Challenge: Legacy code that had been dormant for 2+ years made it difficult to identify all interconnected components Impact Assessment Service Availability: Commercial quote service payment processing disrupted Customer Experience: Unable to process policy payments until resolution Resolution Actions Taken Immediate Fix: Updated the orphaned business rule to explicitly use the 'v3' payment implementation Verification: Confirmed payment processing restoration across all affected endpoints Preventive Measures Short-term Actions: Enhanced Code Review Process: Require specific checklist items for feature flag Recommended Long-term Actions: Feature Flag Lifecycle Management: Establish formal process for feature flag deprecation including: Add Monitoring for unexpected payment gaps: Additional logging and monitoring may be required for ensuring similar problems are caught early Post deployment Issue Policy: Add to the post deployment test verification steps an Issue Policy, with verification that the payment and charge were complete. Lessons Learned Feature flag removal requires the same rigor as feature development - comprehensive impact analysis and testing are essential Legacy system removal is high-risk - systems unused for extended periods accumulate hidden dependencies Test coverage gaps become apparent during cleanup activities and should be addressed proactively.

Problem statement: Guidewire Advance Product Designer outage resulted in Classic PolicyCenter transactions to fail
Description:
• Business Impact: Guidewire Advance Product Designer outage resulted in Classic PolicyCenter transactions to fail
• RCA: APD Deployment to Production and Resulting Instability
A new version of the Advanced Product Designer (APD) service was deployed, resulting in instability that caused the service to become unresponsive to incoming requests.
• Resolution: Implement proposed fix once RCA has been completed.
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2022928. Cause Code: vendor issue. Cause Notes: Multiple customers experienced APD Errors in PolicyCenter Sep 9, 2025 Knowledge Article Number 000045664 Title Multiple customers experienced APD Errors in PolicyCenter Problem Description Customers were unable to perform policy transactions in PolicyCenter and were experiencing APD connectivity errors. Environmental Conditions PolicyCenter Advanced Product Designer Cause 1. APD Deployment to Production and Resulting Instability A new version of the Advanced Product Designer (APD) service was deployed, resulting in instability that caused the service to become unresponsive to incoming requests. 2. Surge in Retries from PolicyCenter to APD PolicyCenter, which depends on APD for product definitions and editions during policy servicing, is configured to automatically retry requests if it receives error responses or timeouts from downstream services such as APD. Due to the APD service instability, a significant number of requests from PolicyCenter to APD failed. Each failure triggered PolicyCenter’s retry logic, resulting in a rapid and repeated surge of retry attempts. 3. Unhealthy APD database The compounded effect of thousands of failed requests and their subsequent retries led to a dramatic increase in the number of concurrent database connections and queries. The database, already handling usual traffic, became overwhelmed by this sudden spike in the load. This additional stress further degraded the performance of both APD and PolicyCenter Resolution 1. APD Code Reversion To immediately address the issue, Guidewire reverted the APD service to the previous stable version as a precautionary countermeasure. The rollback was performed to eliminate any potential impact from the recent changes and to help restore service stability as quickly as possible 2. APD Database Upsizing Despite the code reversion, the system continued to experience significant performance issues due to a surge in retries from PolicyCenter to APD, which had overwhelmed the APD database with excessive connections and queries. The decisive resolution came when the APD database was scaled up to a larger configuration. This increase in database capacity absorbed the ongoing high load, enabling both APD and PolicyCenter to recover normal operations and fully stabilized the environment. Additional Information Corrective and Preventative Measures 1. Guidewire has aligned the future deployment schedule for APD with the Guidewire Maintenance Window. 2. Guidewire is reviewing the current testing scope for APD releases and will extend it as needed to further strengthen quality assurance. 3. Guidewire is also continuing its analysis of the recent APD code release to pinpoint the exact root cause of the issue. While we are confident in our current findings, we are conducting additional root cause analysis to gain deeper insight into why the database was overwhelmed. This includes a thorough review of the PolicyCenter retry mechanism as well as a detailed examination of APD database sizing. These efforts are aimed at ensuring we fully understand all contributing factors and can implement effective measures to prevent similar issues in the future. 4. Guidewire has planned enhancements to the observability of the APD database to provide greater visibility into its performance and behavior. Problem statement: Multiple Applications Inaccessible
Description:
• Business Impact: Multiple applications across the enterprise are experiencing connectivity issues when connecting via the Ashburn Gateway. 
• RCA: > We upgraded the firewalls "ashcloudfw1/2, ashedgefw1/2" to version 11.1.6-h10 as per Palo vendor suggested. After upgrade we lost BGP connectivity "BGP Peering lost" 
-> We downgraded the firewalls to older version "10.2.13-h7" but still BGP sessions didn't establish
-> In ASHEDGE Firewall: We found out BGP sessions are not being established in forwarding table and added Static route "10.184.0.0/15" manually as they are not being learnt        dynamically.
-> We opened a TAC case with Palo and still they are investigating the version bugs. We anticipate it is a Software OS issue, once I get more information from TAC, I'll pass on the information to Problem management team.
-> The BGP peering session between the two firewalls has a hard-coded limit of 5,000 routes (which is the default, but can be increased). We are at that limit – there is 5,000+ routes being advertised, and the route we "dropped" happened to be one of the unlucky ones that didn't make it in the first 5,000.
• Resolution:-> Once static route is implemented, connections started restored.
-> CHG2170281 is successfully completed for enabling the BGP peering session prefixes from 5000 to unlimited. I can see the active BGP sessions in the route table and local RIB. Claims, Net-routers also validated and everything looks good.  
-> Moving forward, we will be doing health checks on every firewalls for BGP peer -Groups setting the limit from 5000 to unlimited for next software patches.

Problem statement: CFRPS-356: CLPC FOAmFam: In Dwelling screen - Coverage A, the Loss Settlement Value dropdown is not filtering correctly for dwellings built in 1940 or earlier.
Description:
Description: CLPC FOAmFam: In Dwelling screen - Coverage A, the Loss Settlement Value dropdown is not filtering correctly for dwellings built in 1940 or earlier.

As per the requirement, the dropdown should only display the following options:
1)Actual Cash Value
2)Functional Replacement Cost

Root Cause: 
The method populateCovALossSettlementValue does not refresh when the Year Built is initially entered as 1940 or earlier.

Working Scenario: If the Year Built is first entered as a value greater than 1940 initially, and then changed to 1940 or earlier, the method is triggered and the dropdown updates correctly.

Non-Working Scenario: If the Year Built is entered as 1940 or earlier initially, the method is not triggered, resulting in the dropdown not refreshing.

Workaround (UI Steps):
1)Click Edit on the selected dwelling.
2)In the Basics tab, change the existing Year Built to a value greater than 1940.
3)Navigate to the Coverage tab.
4)Return to the Basics tab and update the Year Built to 1940 or earlier.
5)You should now see the correct dropdown options under Coverage A (Loss Settlement Valuation).
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2023902. Cause Code: software issue. Cause Notes: Root Cause: The method populateCovALossSettlementValue does not refresh when the Year Built is initially entered as 1940 or earlier..

Problem statement: GCP MuleSoft Project network slowness. Image pulls are dead slow.
Description:
Very high latency in Mulesoft platform hosted in GKE Cluster - gcp-ent-mulertf-preprod & gcp-ent-mulertf-prod

The impact is very high as Kubernetes may restart any Production APIs any time and the API will be down for a long.
Cause notes: From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2022750. Cause Code: software issue. Cause Notes: WHAT WE KNOW SO FAR:Event OverviewA network congestion incident occurred, starting on 8/13 ~0950 until 8/14 ~1040, when multiple Cribl hosts (4+) simultaneously initiated large data transfers to the GCP East region, overwhelming the 2G network link capacity. This created a cascading failure that impacted the entire GCP East region network infrastructure.Technical Sequence of Events 1. Multiple Cribl hosts began transmitting large data volumes concurrently, quickly saturating the 2G GCP East region link beyond its capacity threshold. 2. As the link reached full utilization, the network infrastructure responded normally by dropping packets to prevent complete failure. 3. The TCP protocol's built-in reliability mechanism detected the dropped packets and automatically triggered retransmissions from each source host. This standard behavior inadvertently amplified the problem: - Each retransmitted packet added additional load to the already saturated link - Multiple hosts simultaneously retransmitting created exponential traffic growth - The cycle perpetuated as new retransmissions were also dropped and required further retransmissions 4. This exponential retransmission behavior created a Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) scenario that extended far beyond the original Cribl traffic: - Cribl hosts lost their own transmission capability - All on-premises applications communicating with GCP experienced degraded performance - All GCP applications attempting to communicate with outside application(s) (e.g., Reltio → Mulesoft integrations) experienced timeouts and severe latencyThis chart shows the above behavior and the ensuing exponential retransmission behavior by the offending hosts:RECOMMENDATIONS: TO AVOID FUTURE REPEAT OF THE SCENARIODon't allow multiple hosts to transmit large volumes simultaneously.Implement throttling - Control transmission rates at source hostsSchedule wisely - Use off-hours and alternating schedules for large data transfersAvoid creating DDoS scenarios - Even during off-hours, uncontrolled simultaneous transfers can impact critical workflows like backupsAvoid #1 behavior at all costs!This is a classic example of the network congestion collapse phenomenon where well-intentioned applications can inadvertently create cascading performance issues... 09/04/2025 09:04:19 - venkatesan.manoharan@amfam.com (Work notes)
There are two validations happen from PMAC system for an agent to issue a policy in the current system.

1. Agent should have necessary permission to issue a policy for the specified state.
2. The Producer code which the agent is tagged to should have permission to issue a policy for the state.

We didn’t had the producer code being sent in the request earlier and we added that recently into the request and had a script parameter(EnableOnBehalfOfProducerCodeForLicensingCheck) added to disable or enable it.  By default, EnableOnBehalfOfProducerCodeForLicensingCheck is set to ‘False’. So, if its false we wouldn't send the extra tag of producer code in request and PMAC. This enables PMAC to validate without producer code check and give response as ‘Authorized’ if the agent is valid. Ideally as per latest discussions it has been said that PMAC would need both agent and producer code to be valid to give authorization. But looks like PMAC is still allowing requests without producer code.

On the above understanding, Few months back, we had this script parameter being removed as part of this cleanup card, [CFRFARM-28287] License Check OnBehalfCode Failing - Jira. After this change we are always sending the request with Agent and producer code and PMAC validates for both and even if Agent has access and producer code doesn’t it throws ‘Not Authorized’.

  2. FQDN-dallpanlog01.amfam.com

Adding to the delay in resolving the issue was an issue Thursday morning where the EDC had network links going down so that took us down the incorrect path initially by focusing on the network.

We also saw the next morning that the same block was occurring, so we added the additional IP address to it. This is the permanent fix.

In 'PolicyChangeDiffTreeMapper.gs' file the variable modifier = child.Children.single() is causing the 'java.lang.IllegalStateException: This iterable has more than one element in it'.
When there is a change in the modifier values in the policy change transaction, there are duplicates coming in variable diffTableEntries of function getDiffTable in the 'PolicyChangeDiffTreeMapper.gs' file.

Proposed fix: Might have to fix the logic of handling the list in 'PolicyChangeDiffTreeMapper.gs' file.
(Please note that this is a common code that is used for all LOBs, make sure the fix we are doing doesn't impact other LOBs.)

Problem statement: TR- Relate Wave 4B - Error message when call came through.
Description: Error message when call came through. Relate Wave 4B
Cause notes:
I wanted to provide an update on the ongoing efforts by our project team and IT to troubleshoot and resolve the error experienced by Relate users where they are on queue and unable to answer an incoming call. We are making significant progress and feel confident it is stemming from following issues:
 
  1. Meraki Template Issue: The Meraki template that was originally applied to all users at the start of 4b triggers the internet drop resulting in the error. Template update was pushed end of day 1 of the 4b go-live and successfully resolved this issue for the majority of users.
  2. Microphone Permissions in Browser: Incorrect settings of permissions on the Relate and Media Helper tabs created issues that caused this error to populate for various users. Users should ensure microphone permissions are enabled in both the Relate tab and the Media Helper tab, to avoid disruptions.
  3. Timeout Error: The Media Helper, running in a separate tab, is timing out due to inactivity for over an hour, which is the default setting for Edge tabs. This occurs when representatives have low call volumes or return from breaks/lunch. The Media Helper is designed to operate in the background, hence the inactivity leading to timeouts.
Planned Fixes for Wave 5:
  • Meraki Template Update: We will push the Meraki template update to all users. Steve is coordinating with Tom Sundling to replicate the successful approach used for Wave 4b across all Wave 5 users.
  • Shelf Article Updates: We will enhance the clarity of microphone permission instructions in both Relate and Media Helper to ensure users have a better understanding.
  • Automatic Timeout Settings Update: Chris is working with the end-user computing team to pilot an automatic update to be pushed out to 4b users for timeout settings via specific URLs. Once assessed, this will be rolled out to all users before Wave 5.
We will share more details regarding the planned fixes as they are available! We are all excited to have identified these issues and hopefully mitigate these concerns for Wave 5. 
Thanks!
Aly

Root Cause Analysis: AWS MFA Failure - pgac.com Domain
Date: June 12, 2025
Incident ID: INC4534612

Date of Incident
June 12, 2025

Impacted System
AWS login via Office 365 MFA integration

Primary Domain
pgac.com

***********************************************************************************************************
Root Cause:

Expired RADIUS authentication certificates on the NPS server (PGACAWSMFA01.pgac.com) used
to validate MFA requests from Office 365 to AWS. The expired certificate caused failures with
ESTS_TOKEN_ERROR.
Contributing Factors
- No alerting or monitoring was configured for NPS certificate expiration.
- Nobody had access to the admin account in AWS to troubleshoot with until much later
- Microsoft's certificate renewal process had changed and required updated tooling.
- Firewall denied traffic on port 389 (LDAP) and AWS endpoint IPs during the incident.
- No current staff had full credentials or documentation for the integration.
Key Evidence
- Event Log from PGACAWSMFA01 (1:07PM, 6/12/2025) showed ESTS_TOKEN_ERROR and
certificate validation failure.
- Firewall logs showed denied traffic on LDAP and AWS endpoint IPs.
- Azure sign-in logs showed successful MFA but blocked downstream authentication.
- Zscaler/VPN and PowerShell logs confirmed network path tests and failures.
Resolution
- Updated Microsoft tooling installed on both NPS servers.
- Certificates were renewed and bound to the RADIUS role.
- Firewall rules were corrected to allow required ports/IPs.
- AWS access was restored and login confirmed through testing.
Preventive Actions
- Enable certificate expiry alerting for all RADIUS/MFA endpoints.
- Maintain updated process documentation for Azure MFA/NPS integrations.
- Assign role-based access and credential continuity.
- Implement scheduled test logins to detect early integration failures.

Cause Notes:

Amfam opened Zendesk ticket #23826 at 12:04 PM ET. The ThreatX SOC confirmed unhealthy sensor instances and escalated to ThreatX Engineering. Investigation revealed that sensors could not establish connections to ThreatX Gateway and therefore could not download configuration or certificates. Rolling restarts of the affected Gateways restored stable connectivity by 03:07 PM ET.

Current analysis by the ThreatX SOC indicates that the incident stemmed from a communication failure between the ThreatX sensor and its upstream gateway (controlled by ThreatX). When the secure control channel between these components became unstable, the sensor could not retrieve updated certificate data or configuration changes. As a result, it defaulted to the built‑in self‑signed certificate and intermittently returned HTTP 503 responses.

Problem statement: ForgeRock Release
Description:
ForgeRock was put into production on 05/17 and since then we are seeing Issues with MyAccount - Login, Password Reset and Primary Email Change 

1) Login issues are being faced by 'imported' or 'pending' customers to FR OR 
Customers who haven't logged-in in last 2 years - workaround for these customers is to re-enroll

2) Password Reset Issues are caused because email is not being received by the customer(s). Possible causes could be one of or combination of -
Customer is using incorrect email than the primary email And/Or 
Unable to access email And/Or 
Email address is on hold due to repeated bounces

3) Unable to change email because 
Customer has forgotten their password + has no access to Primary email in use currently
Unable to login to "Make Primary" (refer to point#1 scenarios)
Does not have a secondary email in Relate
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2021996

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

Below are the issues why we are seeing a spike in tickets after ForgeRock implementation - 

1. Before ForgeRock, customers could login using UserID or Email as username along with a password. With ForgeRock, we removed the userID option. Customers need to login  using their email and password. Most of the times, they don't remember the email associated with their MyAccount
2. There was no proactive communication to customers that we are switching from userID to Email. This was a deliberate decision by Product team
3. We only imported customers who created an account or logged in during the last 2 years. Anyone who did not login in the last 2 years or did not create account within last 2 years were not imported into ForgeRock and are not able to login. They need to recreate their account
4. There are multiple issues with customers not being able to reset their password
   a. They were not imported into ForgeRock due to 2 year cutoff
   b. They don't know which email is associated with their account and are using incorrect email for reset password. In this case, they will not receive email with reset pwd link
   c. There is an option to resend email to reset their password. They click the link multiple times and get multiple emails. Then they don't know which one to use. They need to click the most recent email. If they do not, it will expire all the links. We are putting in a fix for both these issues - removing Resend Email button to stop them from sending multiple emails and to expire all links if they click the incorrect one. If they click an older one, it is not expire the most recent reset password link.
   d. The reset password link is a single use link. Sometimes with link scanners, the email client (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook etc) will "click" the link to make sure there is no malicious content. When the customer actually clicks this link, they get an error saying the link is expired. We are putting in a fix for this as well to not expire the link until customer actually changes password or if the link is more than 10 minutes old.
   e. We are seeing email bounces for some providers. We are getting a list from SFMC team and having them resend the email
   f. Comcast customers are not receiving our email because Comcast is not sending the email. This is a know issue and SFMC team is working with our Email reputation vendor.
Close notes: Fix deployed to Prod. We are seeing significant reduction in errors for Reset password.

From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2021949

Cause Code:

Cause Notes:

Good Morning Emily.

 

Thanks for filing the incident regarding Rental Exposure routing. 

 

We did some follow up and can see that the Intake team put in some modifications to the license states with the May ClaimCenter release. 

 

Here is the change that was requested.

We need these states added to the State License: AK, AL, AZ, HI, ID, MN, ME, CA, IN, MI, MS, MT, NC, NV, NY, OR, UT, and WA

 

Since that day, they have been seeing some issues and have made some changes to the states impacted. 

 

As of 5/28, they idenfied an issue and made a modification. 

 

Here was the reasoning. 

On 5/28/2025, it was identified that the states AL, AZ, HI, ID, MN, ME, and CA, which were added to the "state license required" parameter, mandate licenses only for residents.

On that day, they pulled those states back and are now not License required.  

 

I think this explains the increased traffic to the Rental Proxy this week and why it is now back to normal. 

 

 

If you agree, I’m going to close the problem we opened down as the Intake team has made long term corrections to address the issue. 

 

Please let me know your thoughts. 

Thank you

Problem statement: CFRFARM-29278:  FARM Heating Installed/Last Updated Year is Updating when heating systems interchanging rows
Description:
Description:  In Dwelling screen, under Systems, we have Heating Information, There Heating Year is getting updated when Heating Systems are interchanging their rows.

Root Cause: Quote is considering Heat Installed Year of that heating system whichever is coming on first row. If rows get flipped over transaction, Heat Installed Year also gets flipped and impacts rating.

In FRDwellingHeatingSystemsAFIDV.pcf Heating year value is set with dwelling.Building.Heating.YearAdded, Here we are not checking the conditions for primary and secondary heating systems Hence while flipping it is taking whatever value is present top of the Table.

Workaround: N/A

Recreate Step: Create Submission and add two heating systems.
                                  Create policy change on it, when values are flipping, Heating Year value is getting updated with the first heating system year.
Cause notes:
Quote is considering Heat Installed Year of that heating system whichever is coming on first row. If rows get flipped over transaction, Heat Installed Year also gets flipped and impacts rating.

In FRDwellingHeatingSystemsAFIDV.pcf Heating year value is set with dwelling.Building.Heating.YearAdded, Here we are not checking the conditions for primary and secondary heating systems Hence while flipping it is taking whatever value is present top of the Table.

• Caused by Change: No

Workaround:
<RCA> Over 90+ Linux servers that had trouble remounting; NOTE: Virtual servers were all ok

    1. Root Cause: As part of the defined script to remount all servers, the script was unable to trigger Sudo commands due to missing data under unixadm_prod. Also, the local copy of these files was present and used for remounting over 1800 Linux servers but was removed before the remounting process finished (still need to determine why), and was unavailable to remount the final 90+ servers. Once the local file was gone, the script tried to use the central version of the required file from NAS share, but the key file was missing from the NAS share (this was due to the missing share data as noted in the root cause noted above (called ‘Empty NAS shares’).  The local copy of sudoers is required until the link file to /nfs/celadm is created. However, the team attempted to create the link file post moving the local sudoers. Therefore, the new sessions failed to acquire sudo privileges and failed to create link file. While mounting on a set of servers, team triggered the commands such as "mv /celadm /celadm_bkp; ln -s /nfs/celadm /celadm" separately via Ansible shell command.  One member of the Linux team did not follow the process of executing both remounting commands in one session.  This is a process & training issue.
    2. Possible areas for improvement to missing files and/or process-related issues:
  • Ensuring that the local copy remains in place for the entire remounting process (so that you are not dependent on central files).  To accomplish this, all team members performing the remounting need to be trained and must follow the defined process for remounting.  In this case, all resources must know that the process so that both commands for remounting are triggered in one session.

Cause Code:
security issue

Cause Notes:

TG application behind wws.pgac.com was actively being attacked on Saturday, May 3rd.  The attack appeared to be a credential stuffing attack coming from various IP addresses around the country.  A Sev1 incident was opened to address the security attack.  Rules were added in an attempt to block the malicious attack traffic.  Rule additions were agreed to by participants in the Sev1 outage bridge.  Two rules ended up being added that blocked legitimate traffic when legitimate users attempted to access the site on the following Monday.  One was the rule "920046    Block Okhttp for wws.pgac.com".  The development team confirmed that connections using the user agent Okhttp should not be hitting their website so it was blocked for the wws.pgac.com site in ThreatX.  This blocked attack traffic on Saturday but ended up blocking legitimate traffic on Monday.  The Okhttp user agent is used on some Android devices. 

The second rule that ended up blocking legitimate traffic was the "920047    Block Malicious TLS Fingerprint wws.pgac.com attack".  This fingerprint was used heavily by the attacker on Saturday so it was blocked.  It turns out that this fingerprint is used in some Android device versions and is not unique to the attacker.  This rule blocked some Android devices from access websites in the AmFam tenant in ThreatX.
Close notes: Both rules listed above (920046 - Block Okhttp for wws.pgac.com & 920047 - Block Malicious TLS Fingerprint wws.pgac.com attack) were removed from ThreatX to address the issues with some Android devices not being able to access the wws.pgac.com website and websites under the AmFam tenant in ThreatX.

Problem statement: Horison and OLS Performance Issues
Description:
• Business Impact: Agents are reporting OLS and Horison performance issues 
• RCA: It has been noted that elevated memory utilization on the MSMQ and DMMQ servers listed below contributed to the service disruption.
ASGMARMSDMMQ11,ASGMARMSDMMQ12,ASGMARMSMQ12,ASGMARMSMQ11 and ASGMARMSMQ13 servers.

• Resolution: Increase in Memory and CPU size on OLS servers has been completed.
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2021662

Cause Code:
hardware issue

Cause Notes:

It has been noted that elevated memory utilization on the MSMQ and DMMQ servers listed below contributed to the service disruption on following ASGMARMSDMMQ11,ASGMARMSDMMQ12,ASGMARMSMQ12,ASGMARMSMQ11 and ASGMARMSMQ13 servers.

The MSMQ queue depth count was significantly elevated, exceeding 300,000 queues on the DMMQ11 server, as the DMMQ11 (ibills) server reached their maximum queue capacity.
Close notes:

Problem statement: CFRFARM-28830:  FARMOWNERS:  Schedule of Outbuilding Structure type is being selected as 'Dairy Barn' even though different value was selected in value 360.
Description:
Description: Schedule of Outbuilding Structure type is being selected as 'Dairy Barn' even though different value (General Use / Livestock Barn) was selected in value 360.
 
Root cause: For "General Use / Livestock Barn" we're receiving "LVB" value code from value 360 in getValuationReportResponse. Since "LVB" is not configured in fusion and If system is unable to find the type using 360 response, it's defaulting it to Dairy Barn.
 
Workaround: Possible workaround is to temporarily enable script parameter 'EnableAFOCovGStructure' to true temporarily and set the outbuilding structure type value from the drop down.

Steps to Replicate:
1) Navigate to Outbuildings - add new outbuilding and select multistructure. 
2) Click on "Open 360 value"
3) Fill the information for outbuilding structure and give 'General Use / Livestock Barn' for type and click confirm.
Cause notes:
For "General Use / Livestock Barn" we're receiving "LVB" value code from value 360 in getValuationReportResponse. Since "LVB" is not configured in fusion and If system is unable to find the type using 360 response, it's defaulting it to Dairy Barn.

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

System is trying to find outbuilding structure type based on the verisk 360 response. If system is unable to find the type using 360 response, it's defaulting it to Dairy Barn.

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

A significant number of internal AmFam users started testing from inside AmFam. Testing from inside AmFam, those routes go out through Zscaler and are represented externally with Zscaler IPs. That process generated a situation that then tripped rules that eventually blocked those Zscaler IP addresses. Previously, Zscaler IPs being block in the hs_west_cl_2 tenant had not been an issue and as a result, the Zscaler HUB IPs had not been whitelisted for this tenant in ThreatX.  


From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2021437

Cause Code:
vendor issue

Cause Notes:

The root cause of the April 15th was due to the GeoBlocking rule blocking 132 IP addresses, 1680 time. This issue was with a geolocation mismatch in the Maxmind lite Geo database used by the ThreatX sensors. The Maxmind Geo database is a less reliable than the original version and that database contained Zscaler IPs that were blocked as a result.
Close notes: The Zscaler HUB IPs have been removed from the "hs_west_cl_2" tenant.

Problem statement: Issue with Security Group/Role Management Catalog Item workflow
Description:
When updating an Entra group through the Security Group/Role Management catalog item the workflow goes out to find the Entra owners and sends approval. The approval process is wonky where sometimes it will not work on submission. Looks to be when a Entra group owner is the one that puts in the request. Our theory is that its most likely due to having multiple owners for an Entra group. 

Part 2 of the issue is there is no ability to test this issue in Servicenow lower environments due to the fact that we do not have a Ent group preprod instance to connect to. Its only available in Prod. We need to come up with a solution to allow us to handle any type of incidents investigation or even future catalog updates that involve the Entra Security groups.

From Incident:
"When submitting requests through the Security Group/Role Management form such as to update an automation for an Entra group, if you are the owner/approver of the group, the request sometimes gets cancelled as rejected automatically.  This can be seen in RITM2822557 where SNOW shows "Requestor is approver, approving" and the next step is it cancels the request as approver rejected.  It sometimes takes 2-3 submissions before it actually goes through."

Problem statement: CFRFARM-28392: Farmowners-"Location added to the policy. Upload a diagram showing the layout of the farm. (CFRU600859)". while clicking on Request Approval
Description:
Description: Getting a warning "Location added to the policy. Upload a diagram showing the layout of the farm. (CFRU600859)" while clicking on Request Approval button

Root-cause: TC_DEFAULT is meant to be a warning, not a hard stop, but if it's on the button's OnAction, the system is not registering that the warning has already been shown. When the button is clicked again, it re-evaluates the OnAction, triggering the warning again and again, making it behave like a hard stop.
 
The first time the validation triggers, it should warn the user but allow the action to proceed when retried. However, since OnAction re-triggers the validation each time, the warning never gets marked as "acknowledged."

From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2021293

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

 

Root-cause: TC_DEFAULT is meant to be a warning, not a hard stop, but if it's on the button's OnAction, the system is not registering that the warning has already been shown. When the button is clicked again, it re-evaluates the OnAction, triggering the warning again and again, making it behave like a hard stop.
 
The first time the validation triggers, it should warn the user but allow the action to proceed when retried. However, since OnAction re-triggers the validation each time, the warning never gets marked as "acknowledged."

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

-SAPI Offers (a Spring boot AWS hosted service), container went down on 3/28 Friday midnight.

-The root cause was a deployment issue on 3/20 SAPI release where SAPI Offshore team was not able to confirm whether deployment succeeded for this service.

-They assumed it was successful, and it went unnoticed. Partner team informed that Sales Quotes for DMP flow were affected and B2B team informed SAPI team on Sunday 3/30 afternoon and with help from Devops team, SAPI team redeployed the service which fixed the issue.

-The Prod deployment team generally uses the latest commit id from the main branch to create RLS tags. There was an incorrect commit id used for creating the first RLS tag for offers. After realization, it was closed in between, and the correct commit id was used for the tag creation.
 
-The gitlab pipeline passed with a general warning on the last ecs_deploy stage. Since it was a warning, we ignored it but it was the root cause for failure as there was a commit id collision and the ecs tried to spin up the server with the latest commit but a steady state was never achieved.
 
-When it was caught postproduction analysis, the fresh restart resolved it.

Description:
Description: Getting "Document Search Failed. Try again later." while clicking on Request Approval button

Root-cause: Connected with Naveen Kondeti and he advised to create a PRB as he said Tyrell Capers gonna fix this defect. Let me update more to the root-cause as we gather more information

Workaround: To turn off EnableAFOPhotoDocValidation script parameter till the time we fix this issue

There are 3 different issues all being tied to this PRB.
1.  Documents are added, but when the user Refreshes, they receive a SEARCH FAILED message.  They are there.  The user can scroll to the Documents page and find/see them. This appears to be a callout to Nuxeo issue. INC4394321 as an example

2.  Documents are added but when the user attempts to escalate to the UW they receive a detailed HARD STOP (red) that the "correct" type of documents are not loaded, i.e., there's something there, but it's not what we're looking for to meet the set conditions.  INC4387308 as an example

3. Documents are added but when the user attempts to submit to the UW they receive a generic SOFT STOP (yellow) that the correct documents are missing. Typically soft stops allow the user to click on CLEAR and continue down their path.  In this case, it continues to fire and will not let the user past. INC4394326 as example.

These may or may not be related to same root cause, but they are all resolved with the disabled script parameter.  If they are found to NOT be related, we'll need to fix the INC->PRB association.

Problem statement: Multiple Desk Review Services being created on Digital Claims - BUG CFS-4216
Description: For certain digital claims, when the customer is sending in photos to support their claim and the Desk Review Service is being created, we are seeing that there are multiple services set up.   there should only be one.    in CCC - I have 2 examples 01-008-673387-1 and 01-008-677836
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2021107

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

When the photos were uploaded by the customer the system is not recognizing that it has already created a desk review service and it is trying to create another.   when it does, the service is created because of work getting sent to another work queue.   

This is the analysis.  

 

We checked the code, in work queue xml, and we see the class DigitalClmServiceCreatorWorkQueue.gs is being used to create service request for these claims when we receive more than 3 estimate photos for a particular claim, then we start the process. Before upgrade, only one instance/ server was used to process these requests. Now we see that there can be 5 instances at a time. So, for same claim parallel processing is happening which leads to creation of 2 service request at a time. It’s mentioned at the work queue xml that <!--Work queue configuration for Service request creation on Digital claims on receipt of document Do not increase batch size more than 1 since anything greater than 1 would results either in duplicate service request creation or failed to create service request since the parallel processing of workitem would result in incorrect document count in the claim-->

Problem statement: MSA agents are unable to retrieve policy information impacting new and existing policies.
Description:
• Business Impact: MSA agents are unable to retrieve policy information impacting new and existing policies.
• RCA: Teams found that due to Expired Certificate not able to be properly processed. 
• Resolution: Teams performed Renewal of the cert which was verified restored with end users.
• Preventable: Yes
• Caused by Change: No




Our Processors are receiving the attached error when trying to process on our Personal Lines Main Street Station platform. Please review and advise.
Cause notes:
INC4380620 was opened on 3/18/25 by our business customers (ICS). They indicated that they were unable to retrieve claims information while processing policies within PLMSS. 

The team was able to see there were errors in the batch report from the Tuesday night. The PLMSS development team reviewed the issue and determined that there was a certificate that was expired for 'amfamhostbridge.msagroup.com.crt'. This is not a certificate that the PLMSS team had documented in our cert store on AWS pertaining to our application.  

These are the error messages the Development team was able to see in the logs:

ERROR: The certificate of ‘amfamhostbridge.msagroup.com’ is not trusted.
ERROR: The certificate of ‘amfamhostbridge.msagroup.com’ hasn't got a known issuer.
The certificate has expired. 

The certificate had expired on 3/15/25. We did not see this issue until Tuesday (3/18/25) because we do not run batch over the weekend and our Monday night batch did not reflect this issue. 

We escalated the issue to a major incident to get the certificate renewed but then to also try to identify who should own this certificate. Hostbridge is used by other MSA applications in addition to PLMSS. However, PLMSS was the only application that reported issues with retrieving claims via the Hostbridge call. 

Once the security team renewed the certificate we were able to test both in Production and QA to prove that it was working as expected. 


From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2020969

Cause Code:
security issue

Cause Notes:

The amfamhostbridge.msagroup.com.crt certificate expired. This server is used by the MSA PLMSS application system to retrieve claims and other data from the mainframe. The certificate expired on 3/15/25. 

PLMSS batch does not run on the weekends so we were not alerted of this until Tuesday 3/18/25. At that point the PLMSS development team reviewed the log files and found the following error messages:

ERROR: The certificate of ‘amfamhostbridge.msagroup.com’ is not trusted.
ERROR: The certificate of ‘amfamhostbridge.msagroup.com’ hasn't got a known issuer.
The certificate has expired 

The incident was escalated to an MI this morning 3/19/25. 

The net routers team renewed the certificate on the amfamhostbridge.msagroup.com server and the application team was able to verify that we were able to retrieve claims information. The certificate has been renewed for one year until 3/2/2026. 

During the meeting there was discussion on who owns this certificate. The certificate was in place since 4/2020 and was owned by an unknown team. The PLMSS team will take ownership of the server/certificate going forward. The team will also need to gain access to the server as those rights currently do not exist.

Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2020337

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

Upon investigation, we identified that the Netlogon service was in a disabled state on both impacted servers. The Netlogon service is essential for secure channel communications between the system and the domain controller, facilitating authentication requests for domain users and services.
The disabled state of Netlogon caused authentication failures, leading to repeated credential prompts when accessing the application. Since the application relies on domain authentication for seamless access, the absence of Netlogon disrupted the authentication handshake between the web server and the domain controller.
Close notes: We enabled the Netlogon service on both impacted servers and ensured it was set to Automatic startup. Post-remediation, the website functioned as expected without prompting for credentials, confirming that the authentication flow was restored successfully.

Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2020285

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

On 2/4/25 at around 8:20 am, a developer started a clean up batch job/script. Previous scripts related to this clean-up ran without issue, but this one caused the ClaimService (https://prdesb.amfam.com/ccx/cc-router/ClaimService/v02) to get overloaded leading to end users getting ClaimService unavailable errors when working on policy changes. When we found out about the timeouts, we suspended the script which lead to the recovery that occurred at 9:13 am.
Close notes:
There is currently a project (Jira E1PTPRG-2960) in development that's going to replace the current ClaimService. This new API should not have the timeout issues that the current ClaimService experiences when too many calls are made to it.

From E1PTPRG-2960:

Current State:

On premise Opermart was designed to collect claims loss information for policy renewal service used by Amfam only. This was designed for Advance policies for Auto, Property, Commercial and workers comp. Opermart has the ability to capture the loss and claim information. Additionally, Opermart covers Stacked and Unstacked claim details. 

Claim Point Intime service (V2) is called by PLPC/CLPC application upon nightly renewal batch operation. This process pulls claims data by Policy Number or Claim Number in distributed SOAP Calls. Generally, process takes 30 to 40 min for all batch. Each output is generated as XML payload.

New Process:

Data team is building the Advance renewal process on Claims Datalake. Based on the current business logic, they will build a PIT data points and embed them under BigQuery views. From BigQuery extract and store the data in DataStore. PLPC team will use the existing API architecture to read the data from DataStore and use it for renewal. The API will be called passing one of the following parameters:

policynumber

claimnumber

load_dt

There will be a separate request/response for each Line of Business (auto, property and commercial). They will not be combined into a single request/response.

Description:

• RCA: Compass changed their authentication from Okta to Entra ID.  Since Claims center also uses Okta for authentication, this could possibly be related, since the issue started in

User is getting SSO Authentication error in Claims
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2020203

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

This is a huge assumption, but last Thursday, Compass changed their authentication from Okta to Entra ID.  Since Claims center also uses Okta for authentication, this could possibly be related, since the issue started in a similar timeline.  The theory continues that possibly something with the authentication became stale, since users are forced to log into compass every time it is opened.  


From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2020203

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

Claims isn’t depending on another application for its authentication token. Rather, the browser stored a token that was no longer valid. There is nothing to fix here on anyone’s side because the issue will never repeat itself in our environment. To understand this, you must understand what the authentication flow was before the compass change and then after the compass change. Without a whiteboard, I’ll attempt to illustrate this.
 
First touch from the browser, by policy, is Compass. The previous flow was:
 
Compass URLOkta IDPEntra ID (for the authentication)Okta IDP (receives authentication token via OIDC)Compass URL (receives SAML assertion)(insert whatever method someone uses to go to Claims)Okta IDP (which has a valid authentication token previously)Claims (receives SAML assertion)Profit…
 
The new flow:
 
Compass URL Entra ID (for IDP and authentication)Compass URL (receives OIDC)(insert whatever method someone uses to go to claims)Okta IDP (does not have a valid authentication)Entra ID (for authentication)Okta IDP (receives previous authenticated assertion)Claims (receives SAML assertion from old, invalid session)No Profit…
 
The problem with the new flow is that SAML assertions are carried by the browser, not by the tools that inject them (such as Okta or Entra). Because Compass was previously using Okta, each time you opened the browser and it took you to Compass, you were creating a new session in both Okta and in Entra. This session was used to build the SAML assertion to Claims when you went to Claims. When Compass moved to Entra only (removing Okta), the session that was created was Entra only (and is a different type of session altogether, OIDC). When the user then went to Compass, that launched a connection to Okta. Since our Okta environment also uses Entra for the authentication, it would redirect the user to Entra only to discover that the user is already authenticated. Okta would then pass the assertion to the browser to pass to Claims. But, because the assertion most likely contains the same session ID that was used when Okta was in front of Compass, it reused a cached session thinking it was valid when it was not. When the assertion was then passed to Claims, Claims rejected it because it was not the valid session that it was expecting.
Close notes:
When Compass was still using Okta, users would log into Compass each day.  As part of that process it created some type of artifact (maybe a cookie), that then other apps that were also using Okta would use for their authentication, kind of a shortcut.
 
When Compass changed to Entra, the last "artifact" it had created was still there, but became stale.  The other apps, like Claims Center, saw the artifact and tried to use it, like it has in the past but it was no longer valid, so the authentication failed.  By clearing the cache, it gets rid of that artifact, thus forcing the other apps, like Claims Center, to full re-authenticate, which then works.

Problem statement: Multiple users unable to access their VDIs
Description:
• Business Impact: Multiple users experienced issues accessing their Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) through the Citrix application. Sessions will launch and after a couple minutes, the session will fail to connect.
• RCA: Assigned and In progress
• Resolution: Implement proposed fix once RCA has been completed.
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No
Cause notes:
The root cause of the three identified issues appears to be linked to a single “event.” However, the specific event triggering these issues is not yet known. The problems were limited to Windows 11 Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) and impacted only 80 of the 1,690 Windows 11 VDIs in production across AFI, TG, and MSA.

Issue #1: Wave-Like Impact on VDIs

Impact Timeline: Affected VDIs experienced issues in a “wave” pattern. On January 22, a subset of VDIs was impacted, and additional VDIs were affected on January 23. This pattern resembles the behavior of software or an application being installed or activated.

Observations: The affected VDIs experienced 100% CPU usage, rendering them unable to register with support applications or function normally.

Resolution: A reboot of the impacted machines restored functionality. Monitoring of the boot process confirms that windows patching was the major contributing factor to the CPU spikes causing the VDI to become unavailable.

Issue #2: VDI Crashes and Reboots

Cause: This issue was not caused by external interference or platform-level disruptions. Instead, it was due to an application on the Windows 11 VDIs causing the operating system to crash and initiate a reboot.

Logs: Health logs from individual VDIs indicated: “The VM has received a reboot request from an authorized user or process.”

Issue #3: Microsoft Teams Crashing VDIs

Impact: Some users were unable to launch Microsoft Teams, as the application crash caused the VDI to lose connection and reboot.

Cause: This issue was not the result of external interference or platform errors. The exact reason Microsoft Teams began crashing is unclear, and the total number of affected users is unknown. There is a possibility that external software contributed to the crashes.

Problem statement: CFRFARM-25327: The enhancement made for a free form text box on creating documents no longer works.
Description:
Description : As part of CFRFRMPRG-823 a free form text box was created for our users. At some point in the recent past this enhancement went away. We need to reinstate it.
This is in PolicyCenter.

Root cause : The field related to the enhancement -> "Add policy change summary" checkbox along with text area input will appear only when the logged in user has the "EDITPOLICYCHANGESUMMARY_AFI" permission.
Currently in prod none of the roles has this permission which is the reason the field is not displaying on screen.
In prodcopy when I added this permission to one of the roles then I am able to see this field.

Workaround : As a workaround we can add back the permission for these roles from UI or backend af_admin_shared_svc2,mga_producer_uw, msa_uw_fr
