Problem statement: Major Incident | Functions in Policy Center are returning errors
Description:
• Business Impact: End users are getting ClaimService timeouts when trying to get updated claims information.
• RCA: Software issue/ Since the beginning of January, MDM/Reltio is updating customer preference information for their privacy optout settings. This is updating hundreds of thousands of contacts per day and sending these updates to downstream systems like PLPC. Normal volume of contacts updates per day before this process started was less than 30,000 per day. This causes PLPC to create and process a lot more workflows than normal since every contact update we receive will create a workflow to check if any of the contact's policies need to be updated. These additional workflows delayed the processing of our renewal workflows which call the ClaimService as part of their processing. If there are too many calls to the ClaimService at one time, PLPC will start to receive timeout errors which can happen if renewal workflows are processing at the same time users are trying to work on other transactions like policy changes. 
• Resolution: Implemented CHG2147338, the MDM/Reltio made a change to stop sending these type of contact updates to downstream. 
• Preventable: No
• Caused by Change: No

Problem statement: Errors When Quoting at The General
Description:
• Business Impact: Errors When Quoting at The General

• RCA: The clearing of the flag caused the credit to not get correctly applied on quotes. Without credit, the rater fails one of its first steps which is to determine acquisition cost. This results in the error "Rater is unable to determine acquisition cost amount in file PALACQ. (RAT4001) ."


• Resolution:  Ensure a valid value exists for all 3.9 business for PALRBC.RCCREDIT. It has been communicated to the tables team. There should be no reason in the future for a similar change request as its a one time change. Additionally, there is an app to build PALRBC for 3.9 conversions going forward that forces a valid value to be entered into the table.

• Preventable: Yes

• Caused by Change: Yes/CHG2147028
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2019720

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

Upon further analysis, the clearing of the flag caused the credit to not get correctly applied on quotes. Without credit, the rater fails one of its first steps which is to determine acquisition cost. This results in the error "Rater is unable to determine acquisition cost amount in file PALACQ. (RAT4001) ."


1) What caused this to have major incident impact?

The PALRBC.RCCREDIT field was cleared as part of change request PSSI-2170. In a meeting on 1/9/25 with various members of the business and IT, it was discussed this field would no longer be used as it’s only been used for renewals historically. https://amfament.atlassian.net/browse/PSSI-2170

2) How can this be prevented from reoccurring?
This change was unique in nature in that a segment of business was brought into compliance. There would be no reason to make a change like this again in the future. As a precaution though, it has been communicated to the tables team that this field needs to always have a valid value.

3) Do any process or procedures need to be updated to account for whatever caused the Major Incident, or any other guardrails put in place?
No, as stated in the previous question, this was a one-time change and there would be no reason for a similar change in the future.

4) Is there a Problem Record associated with this, and has it been resolved?
No, this is the first and last change of this nature. Yes, it has been resolved. PALRBC.RCCREDIT now has a valid value.

5) This is the 2nd time this Template has caused an MI (Previously in 2023: CHG2100261 / INC3480475 / PRB2007705). Is the cause the same as last time?

No, CHG2100261 was due to the accidental miss of moving a table from test to production for a routine rate revision.

CHG2147028 was due to a one-time change updating a field that has only been historically used for renewals to bring a segment of business into compliance.
Close notes: This was a one time change that would not be made in the future.

Problem statement: [ECD-14611] Limitation on the utility that creates the Merge batch file (results in the file not getting the accounts in the file even though MR01 is present)
Description:
The utility that is used to generate the merge batch file seems to have an issue where accounts that should be included are not getting included in the file.  Impact is that the user is not seeing the link in the next batch as expected. 

Users are not seeing the View Duplicate link when the accounts should.
Cause notes:
For the ones that appear to be matches based on MR01, but Reltio UI does not display them as matches and neither does the utility picks up as matches, doing some research and working with Reltio I found out that actually the match exists based on MR01, it is just not picked up for initial display on UI or even for the utility for match file. The reason is that there are too many matches based on other rules. The display limits the number of potential matches to be shown and so does utility because of performance reasons. I can show you how to go about confirming it. If we get into a lot of these, we can open a JIRA and look at possibility of updating the utility. That has two cons, one this utility is not supported by Reltio but is like open source contributed and maintained by Reltio community. If we change it, it will become our own version and from then on, we will have to maintain it for any Reltio upgrades. The other is that it will adversely impact performance and if we are planning on doing multiple runs in a day, we will have to be really careful about performance. So, we will have to weigh these against how many of these we run into. Workaround would be to confirm inspecting potential matches a level deeper for these and confirming if these are being flagged as potential matches.

Problem statement: Bloomberg application is down.
Description:
• Business Impact:  Users' inability to access the Bloomberg application.

• RCA: Initial analysis, Teams verified this outage was due to an outage with the Bloomberg primary router. Bloomberg was engaged and had failed over to the secondary router, however the static route on the firewall was set to a physical IP address and need to be reverted back to a virtual address.

• Resolution: Implement proposed fix once RCA has been completed.

• Caused by Change: No
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2019520

Cause Code:
hardware issue

Cause Notes:

Router failure on one leg of redundant MPLS circuits to Bloomberg's network. Surviving router incorrectly configured to function properly in the event of the virtual IP address being inoperative. 


From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2019512

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

The Bloomberg secondary router did not have a return path back to the AmFam network. When the primary went down, all services were down.
Close notes: Bloomberg did not have a return route back to AmFam resources on the secondary router. After adding the 10.0.0.0/8 network to route through the tunnel, service was restored.

On December 12, 2024, between 4:35 PM PST and 8:01 PM PST in the US East (N. Virginia) (US-EAST-1) Region and between 4:48 PM PST and 7:54 PM PST in the Europe (Ireland) (EU-WEST-1) Region, some customer requests to Amazon Cognito APIs failed with the error “TooManyRequestsException” when the customer had not exceeded their quota. All Cognito operations that are not authenticated using AWS IAM [1], such as InitiateAuth and GetUser, were impacted. As a result, customers experienced elevated error rates with operations including user authentication, user data retrieval, and user creation. These operations may have succeeded after one or more retries during that period, and throttling rates returned to normal after the service recovered.

The root cause was a partial update to a Cognito component that manages request quotas and throttling. This update applied stricter limits to all customer requests in the impacted Regions. We use automation to manage the deployment and testing of our service code. One feature of our deployment automation is that test failures in production environments automatically roll the service back to a known-good state. In this case, a defect in our deployment system caused the incorrect partial rollback of a production feature related to throttling enhancements. With the feature in this state, impacted customer requests were not throttled based on individual customer quotas, but based on a protective quota used for requests not attributed to authenticated users. As a result, customer requests that were within a customer’s individual quota were throttled instead when the aggregate call rate in the region exceeded that protective quota.

We were first alerted to the issue when a synthetic monitor failed and paged an service team engineer. We were able to identify the root cause and begin putting in place two mitigations. We raised the protective quota as the fastest potential path to reduce the throttling rate. In parallel, we rolled forward the change that had been incorrectly rolled back in order to restore the previous behavior. The throttling rate reduced as these actions progressed, and the rate returned to normal once the deployment completed.

Cause Notes:

Hope you're doing well. I wanted to share Lindsay's detailed write-up following the investigation of the logs from the AMFAM outage on December 11, 2024. The investigation showed that there were no issues on the CCE side or within CDW's shared datacenter infrastructure for these devices. During the bridge call, the issue resolved itself indicating that the outbound call issue was entirely a carrier problem. If you have any more questions or need further clarification, I can set up a call with you, Lindsay, and myself to discuss further.

Problem statement: [RELATE-23948] Match Rules preventing Account updates
Description:
Match Rules appear to be the same between Add vs. Edit flows. This is resulting in users not being able to make any edits to their customers, because the Add match rules are being applied to their Edits. For comparison, in Apex, Edits invoked their own sets of Match Rules and only returned Exact Matches based on DL or SSN/FEIN (no other fields).

Example:
User edits Person A to enter/update their DL. Upon submitting the change, an Exact Match is found to Person B, who has no DL entered at all but must meet other Add Match Rules to be returned as an Exact Match. Their only choice is to select the match found (Person B). Because a duplicate was found and selected, the DL they are trying to enter is not successfully entered and now exists on either Account. They literally cannot enter it in Relate without entering this circle.

WORKAROUND: PLPC allows them to enter the DL to bypass this roadblock, but they will run into it again on the next edit they attempt in Relate.

Problem statement: Multiple applications seeing consistent alerting
Description:
Business Impact:  Multiple applications seeing consistent alerting.

Root-Cause:  One of the SiteMinder server (psmv017) was seeing large connections.

Resolution: After restarting the policy service both monitoring and connection issues were restored.

Caused by Change: No
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2019288

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

Based on the logs we collected from affected SiteMinder Policy Server (psmv017). we see number of connections to affected SiteMinder Policy Server started increasing on [Mon Nov 25 2024 21:15:01]. From there it keeps growing until [Tue Nov 26 2024 00:20:02]. Usually current connections fluctuate between 2000 - 3000 range and we saw max it went to 4047. But during this MI, we see current connections growing from 2000-3000 range to all the way to 13000. At the same, as current connections keep spiking - Busy Threads also reached to 50 around Mon Nov 25 2024 21:20:01 and stayed at 50 until: [Tue Nov 26 2024 00:20:02]. As the connections keep growing, SM Policy Servers started using all its threads to serve the requests. As connections keep growing, there is no more threads available for the SM Policy Server to use to process the requests which leads to slowness and monitoring start triggering alerts to the applications.

Looking at the logs that we collected during the MI, we seen a thread that got hung when SM policy server is connecting to AppAuth Database. Based on the logs that are available to us, when one of the thread went to hung state, it started increasing the busy threads and and current normal queue depth and that caused slowness in processing the incoming connections and as result connections keep increasing and reached to a point where it can't process the requests intime impacted overall performance of the server.
Close notes: Monitoring is set up on the Siteminder logs to fire an INC if "Current Norm Depth=100*" OR "Busy Threads=5*" meaning if norm Depth > 1000 in busy threads exceeds 50 for 30 minutes.

Problem statement: cannot do a policy refresh on Classic ABEST FR Policy -- BUG: ECI-14177
Description: Claim center will not allow a policy refresh - policy number 22PR206003.  Receiving an error that reads - Render Exception when i try to refresh it
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2019196

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

Reason:

During the Farm 2.0 effort, developers reused the same mapper for Abest and Farm 2.0 policies.

For Abest, the system directly maps the policy type as Farmranch without expecting values from the policy service.

For Farm 2.0, the code searches for the <productName> tag from the policy service to map the policy type in ClaimCenter.

Since Abest uses the same mapper, it also looks for the <productName> tag, which is not provided by the policy service for Abest, causing the code to break.

The Farm 2.0 code changes were reverted from the November release, but this specific change was not reverted.
Close notes: A change was made that allows ABEST policies to call successfully and retrieve policy data

Problem statement: [RELATE-23566] The Accounts selected could not be merged due to conflicting information. Report your issue to FAST if these accounts truly need to be merged.
Description:
This message is expected when the link to do a merge is present but when selecting the second account, there is customer data identified that conflicts and is not meeting the requirements to merge the accounts.

Example - since ethe merge file runs 3 times a day there could be accounts that met the criteria when the file generated but have had updates and now, they no longer meet the criteria so Relate is stops the user from merging.  

This problem will be closed out once the current incidents are closed/resolved. Going forward the Incident triage process should be used to review the conflicts and determine if the issue can be resolved or if it needs to be escalated to the Data Steward/Customer data teams to have the data validated to identify if the merge should be allowed or not.
Cause notes:
There are multiple causes for this issue

  1. Vantage sends the MI in the first name field - CDH/CP had logic that split the MI out to the Middle Name field, but that logic was lost with the new integrations. 
  2. The remaining data conflicts between FN/LN, DOB, Gender, Family Suffix, DL, SSN, FEIN are all meeting original requirements. However, we are opening up a couple rules to reduce the likelihood that a user will be stopped from doing the merge 
    1.  Gender - opening up rule so that if one is populated and the other is not, we won't stop them from merging. (current rule of if they are both populated, they must match remains in place) Relate release on 1/9/25 opened that up, MDM has a story, hope change is in prod between 2/11/25-2/18/25 that when they make the change will make the accounts meet MR01 if one is populated, and the other is not. MDM portion of the work is in S2 and will help the matches be identified earlier.

Problem statement: Multiple Applications Alerting with Issues
Description:
Business Impact: Multiple apps using SiteMinder AUTH was impacted due to the back-end database patching issues.

Root-Cause: DB servers for SiteMinder was patched causing SiteMinder to Panic

Resolution: TBD
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2018294

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

Under ServiceNow Automated Patching window, the attribute “Waiting for Ansible” was set to true for the the DB host pdba239 instead of false. Therefore, the server got included to the 11/17 patching cycle. And the patching process triggered the reboot of the host which in turn caused DB outage.
Close notes: RCA Ptask has been filled with details. Another Ptask has been assigned to SNOW team to understand the reason behind "Waiting for Ansible" flag value change to true.

DBA found that DB instances such as ORAP0038 and ORAP0057 are not online.  DBA tried to bring up the instances however, it didn’t work. Notified Linux team to perform OS level reboot of the host Pdba239 post which the DB instances were brought up successfully.  After completing restarts of affected infrastructure, respective teams validated and confirmed that all impacted applications were functioning as expected.  Linux team engaged Scott Coen and investigated further, during which Linux team found that pdba239 was pulled into 11/17 overnight's patching cycle due to Orchestration issues within ServiceNow.  In general, the "Waiting for Ansible" should be set to true at first and then once the server is included to the patching inventory, the flag value will be flipped to false. However, in this case, the value that Linux team found is 'true' due to which server was included into subsequent patching window. ServiceNow team can determine the root cause for potential issues with orchestration.  Moving forward, Linux team will check the patching window status post patching and ensure the patching lifecycle state is appropriate post successful patching of the Linux servers.

Problem statement: Users experienced some issues with the Fusion app.
Description:
Business Impact: The fusion servers were showing errors in the logs and was not accessible to a few users. 

Root-Cause:  Fusion team identified that after the patching was done, some of the fusion servers were showing errors in the logs, which would impact users to reach the impaired server and experienced some issues with the Fusion application

Resolution: The Fusion team made a change to update the version files to resolve the issue. (CHG2141566) 

 Caused by change: CHG2139021
Configuration item: Commercial Farm Ranch Fusion PolicyCenter - PROD
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2018216

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

The sequence of events leading up to INC4162586 is as follows:
A temporary ratebook file was included by mistake with Fusion PolicyCenter's 10/20 release.
As part of each release we run a batch process to load ratebooks.  This process creates and then deletes temporary files.  The extra temporary file was removed as part of this batch processing.  The file removal did not cause any problems at the time, but left the server running the batch process in a state where it would generate a different checksum at startup.

We did not see any issues after 10/20 because we did not perform any server restarts between 10/20 and 11/3.

On 11/3 Fusion deployed another release, ran the ratebook batch process successfully, on server pclblcob002, cleaned up temporary files, including the one mistakenly included in the 10/20 release.

On 11/10 the Fusion's batch servers were restarted after patching.
pclblcob001 and pclblcob003 went through the normal startup process and started successfully.
pclblcob002 started successfully, but generated a different checksum because the temporary file had been removed.  This triggered a Guidewire upgrade process.
pclblcob004, pclblcob005, and pclblcob006 failed to start because their checksums and versions were behind the new values created by the pclblcob002 upgrade.

Cause Notes:

Dynatrace HTTP monitors triggered the alert for application unavailability. Upon further investigation, teams found that SiteMinder and Auth Applications were unable to connect to the DB instances hosted on DB hosts pdba227 and pdba239.DBA team was in progress of starting the DB services on Pdba239 and Pdba227 post patching when the applications were trying to connect to DB services.

Because sequence #1 of patching window consists of 25 DB servers. Out of which Pdba256 hosting both active/passive DB services gets patched manually as usual.Pdba227 and pdba259: Physical servers didn't boot up within the time limits due to which patching orchestration failed to run remaining tasks. Description:

11/12/2024 12:46:04 - Thomas Janik (Work notes)
It was determined that the issue Thursday night was code in the Dynatrace uninstall script that killed any process using a Dynatrace mount point. All Apache/JVM instances and the Autosys Agent were still being injected for RUM with a library that was loaded from the mount point (occurs until the app restart).  Even though the files were deleted, the processes were still connected to the mount.  The uninstall script had a kill command for any processes that were connected to the mount so the mount could be unmounted.  This was not something Monitoring requested the script to do, nor was it communicated that this code was added to the script. By removing this code (see below) from the script, we saw the Apache/JVM processes continue to run correctly after Dynatrace was uninstalled. After proving this on the CC v8 servers, we ran the new script on papp011 and papp014 (shared pillars servers) and saw none of the JVM/Apache's crash.  We also ran Dynatrace uninstalls on Friday 11/8 on some 1100 more servers with no issues. We did see similar issues like this in preprod and perf.  We reported these issues and asked to see a demo of the fixes before the script was run in prod to avoid this. When we saw the prod demo on 11/6 and received an explanation of the script, it was never once mentioned this unmounting code was added. In hindsight we could have asked to see the literal code during the uninstall demo. We did not. When we were diagnosing the issue after the outage at 2:30am, we did ask to see the code and instantly saw what was wrong.  

… the code removed (kill_process was root cause of JVM/Apaches and Autosys agent coming down):

# Attempt to unmount mount points, force unmount if necessary
for mount in /opt/dynatrace /var/log/dynatrace /var/lib/dynatrace; do
    # Check if the directory is actually mounted before trying to unmount
    if mountpoint -q "$mount"; then
        umount -f "$mount" 2>/dev/null || {
            echo "$mount is busy. Attempting to kill processes using it."
            kill_processes_using "$mount"
            sleep 10  # Wait longer for processes to terminate
            umount -f "$mount" || { echo "Failed to forcefully unmount $mount."; exit 1; }
        }
    else
        echo "$mount is not mounted. Skipping unmount."
    fi
done

… the code removed (kill_process was root cause of JVM/Apaches and Autosys agent coming down):

# Attempt to unmount mount points, force unmount if necessary
for mount in /opt/dynatrace /var/log/dynatrace /var/lib/dynatrace; do
    # Check if the directory is actually mounted before trying to unmount
    if mountpoint -q "$mount"; then
        umount -f "$mount" 2>/dev/null || {
            echo "$mount is busy. Attempting to kill processes using it."
            kill_processes_using "$mount"
            sleep 10  # Wait longer for processes to terminate
            umount -f "$mount" || { echo "Failed to forcefully unmount $mount."; exit 1; }
        }
    else
        echo "$mount is not mounted. Skipping unmount."
    fi
done

Problem statement: Agents are unable to create quotes for new customers through the sales platform
Description:
Business Impact:  Agents were unable to create quotes for new customers through the Personal Lines Policy Center - sales platform

Root-Cause: API Secrets Keys rotated without proper CHG/planning for GCP service account. Process Gap.

Resolution: Implement process change & CHG process embedded in CI/CD pipelines to check for approved Change.
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2018177

Cause Code:
security issue

Cause Notes:

Authentication failures were observed while Mulesoft component that publishes customer information change events from Reltio was trying to access the GCP queues/topics (cust-updates-summary-reltio-gcp-ent, cust-updates-summary-reltio-gcp-ent-sub-mule). That blocked publishing of customer change messages. Consequently, customers created in Relate were not available in Personal Lines Policy Center for Agents to quote sales platform and hence the error (Error -"Could not create the Account" in Producer Engage). The authentication issues were caused by inadvertent rotation of keys for the service accounts associated to the topics/queues mentioned above.

Problem statement: DocumentFederationService -  P8 Documents intermittently inaccessible
Description:
Business Impact:  Agents unable to access policy documents impacted. Application using P8 Document Federation service were seeing errors.

Root-Cause: Middleware servers hosted on IBM WebSphere encountered hung threads (due to long running queries from the back-end database). Long running queries needs to be identified and fine-tuned.

software issue

The JVMS were facing slowness

They had hung threads

based on our research and with analysis from the IBM WebSphere vendor - TS017751209 - we identified there were long running queries causing hung threads
-- To recover the JVMS we performed a clean restart of the WebSphere environment

This needs to be further analyzed by the P8 team/ vendor and provide the problematic queries to the application team for fine tuning and resolution.

The reason is that the code repo which includes the password has the password as incorrect when FE is deployed.

Problem statement: [RELATE-19422] Can't mark deceased if primary and all other HH members are already deceased
Description:
Relate has logic which prevents the Primary Member of a Household from being marked deceased (unless they are the only member). First, they must change the Primary Member to someone else in the household. However, there is also logic which prevents them from making a deceased individual the Primary Member.

Problem statement: Customer Data Hub Services Impacted
Description:
Business Impact:  Customer Data Hub services failing integrating with Comforte and impacting all consumers of CDH services like PLPC, MyAccount, Fusion, Midvale, Salesportal etc

Root-Cause:  Teams found that a vendor issue (Comforte, Inc) with the tokenization and detokenization of data impacted the consumers of the Customer Data Hub service

Resolution: Pending from vendor side RCA
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2017857

Cause Code:
vendor issue

Cause Notes:

  • Comforte is setup in Kubernetes environment on-prem with underline VM.
  • Comforte Pods can restart due various reasons including (however not limited to) patching when underline VMs restart.
  • Once Pods restart, it pulls image (e.g. docker image) from Comforte registry which is hosted on Comforte cloud.
  • As Comforte experienced Infrastructure outage their multiple systems including registry was down, so pods were not able to pull the image and so was in pending state.
  • Pods can not serve requests till it is ready status and so CDH requests were failing.
Close notes: RCA discussed and a task is created to track the solution to closure.

Problem statement: Multiple applications observing disruptions due to Siteminder
Description:
Business Impact:  Multiple services times out causing multiple proposals at once due to Siteminder Socket error 104

Root-Cause: Siteminder internal policy servers took more time to perform auth/authz against Active directory domain (corporate.amfam.com) causing overall slowness and high response times.

Resolution: Increased the number of LDAP banks to 4. Additionally, added the failovers in case of failure on primary LDAP bank. By doing this, SiteMinder Policy Servers can open connections to four LDAP banks to process auth/authz events which helps in overall improvement on the performance across the SM Policy Servers.
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2017865

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

Previously for AD (corporate.amfam.com) connection from SiteMinder Policy Servers, we have four LDAP banks. Over the time three of those LDAP banks are no longer available for SiteMinder Policy Servers as those LDAP banks are decommissioned. All this time, SiteMinder is operating on one connection to corporate.amfam.com which we feel caught up to speed to a point of affecting overall performance of the servers.
Close notes:
corporate AD is one of main user directory that SiteMinder uses to perform Auth/Authz for users and service accounts that uses SiteMinder to access the SM protected apps and API's. From Capacity standpoint, we can't do much. It's already at right capacity. Only thing i can think of bottleneck that caused Auth/Authz events might be the reason for degradation in performance.

we addressed the bottleneck with this change order: CHG2138753

Problem statement: Network Disruption Impacting Multiple Applications at TheGeneral
Description:
Business Impact: Multiple applications at TheGeneral were inaccessible due to a large network disruption.

Root-Cause: As per vendor, HPE, the compute (SY480Gen10 PLUS (S/N: MXQ22410L9 ) that crashed had FCoE configured and therefore was configured for Priority Flow Control (PFC).

Resolution:  Once the RCA is determined, team will work on the permanent solution.
Cause notes:
Working theory, we are waiting for HPE to validate was Host had crashed and its NIC card was sending errors in high enough volume that the interconnect was unable to keep up with the LACP packets to keep the channel up and stable.

 

RCA from HPE 

The compute (SY480Gen10 PLUS (S/N: MXQ22410L9 ) that crashed had FCoE configured and therefore was configured for Priority Flow Control (PFC).
The VC pause flood protection feature was enabled but because PFC was configured it only monitors for a priority pause flood.
When the compute crashed something caused it to send continuous port-level Pause frames instead of priority pause frames.
VC was not monitoring for port-level pause frames yet the VC switch ASIC still was affected by them.
Essentially the port-level pause from the compute that crashed caused VC to send pause frames to the upstream Cisco switch continuously prevent the Cisco switch from sending LACPDUs and LLDPDUs and therefore the LAGs timed out.

We are working with development to see if there is a way to modify the pause flood protection feature to account for this scenario. 

If this is a possibility, it will be included in a future version of the firmware.


From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2017734

Problem statement: Multiple production services are unreachable affecting all enterprise users and some customer functions.
Description:
Business Impact: Multiple production services are unreachable to enterprise users causing issues with customer and internal IVR's, Billing fuctions, and internal applications.

Description:
Business Impact:  Payment Service wasn't available for users in PolicyCenter resulting in users being unable to process policies.

Root-Cause: Due to a release for payment manager, where the proxy JVM was not restarted during the CHG2136021.

Resolution: An Emergency CHG2136104 created to Restarted papp222eg Apache to restore the service.
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2017024

software issue

Cause Notes:

software issue

Cause Notes:

We have Implemented the change TASK - CTASK2068809 and application verification also completed  later on application team requested to restart the papp222eg JVM through emergency change - CHG2136104

 

Additonally,

As explained in the Executive outage following is the details of what occurred, and that Apache webserver was not the actual cause but a residual issue from the release errors.

History:
A payment manager release went in a day before during which an issue was identified and was later fixed by the App team.
Post their fix went in, they also found that this Apache instance is still non-responsive/ throwing errors and needs to be restarted.

Affect on Apache:
During this emergency change it was identified this Apache is facing issues and or is down.
During our analysis we identified that Apache webserver was up and running. However, due to the release errors there may have been bad traffic (incorrect payload, etc.,) caused the instance to misbehave (high resource usage, etc.,) and resulting in unresponsiveness of the webserver issue. This could have been fixed with an Apache restart after the issue fix but that functionality wasn't there in the release jobs.
With the emergency change the specific Apache server instance - papp222eg - in prdeg25 was restarted to fix for the issue.

Follow up:
The payment application release restart job to be modified to include for Apache webserver restarts steps to be added by the app team along with the JVM restarts in that job.

Problem statement: Users reporting connection issues with Zscaler and Global Protect.
Description:
Business Impact: Users reported connection issues with Zscaler
Root-Cause: Based on the initial findings, Zscaler's PAC file logic often uses geo-location to select the nearest gateways, which can lead to both primary and secondary being in the same city if multiple data centers (DCs) are available there. Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016949

Cause Code:

Cause Notes:

United Fiber had a very unique internet routing issue trying to access the ZScaler data center in Chicago.  This was outside of support both ZScaler and internal engineering/support can provide.  Once internet routing was properly restored by them, the issue went away.

From Zscaler Technical Support!
Your scenario makes sense, and you've identified a potential issue with geographical redundancy when both primary and secondary gateways are located in the same city. If there's a regional ISP issue affecting that city, it could indeed prevent traffic from reaching either gateway, causing a connection issue.

Understanding the Issue
Regional ISP Issues: If an end user's traffic cannot reach either the primary or secondary gateway due to an ISP issue affecting the entire region (e.g., Chicago), both gateways could become unreachable.
Geo-Location Based Selection: Zscaler's PAC file logic often uses geo-location to select the nearest gateways, which can lead to both primary and secondary being in the same city if multiple data centers (DCs) are available there.
Potential Solution
Diversify Gateway Locations:
Manual Selection in PAC: Instead of relying solely on geo-location, you can manually configure the PAC file to include gateways from different cities for redundancy.   This will not work for us as we have simplified our PAC's and use subclouds to control access.  I do have a potential mitigation thought but want to think more on it before proposing.  It is centered on only defining a single DC for Chicago and NYC (versus 2 for each) which would then force the secondary gateway thru a different geo-location.  Not "bullet proof" as it depends on the size/scope of an internet outage but would address this unique situation - more to come

09/05/2024 11:47:37 - rene.steele@amfam.com (Work notes)
Update from David B: a little background on the logic ZScaler uses to determine the data center to use.  There is no actual IP ping/probe but strictly uses the geo-ip location of the end users public IP (by longitude/latitude) and selects the closest DC location based on the ZScaler gateway defined in the local PAC file.  In our case, we limit users being within the US to only connect to US-Only DC's (mainly for source-ip application controls).  The every US based user goes to is:    gateway.AmFam-US-Based-Only.zscalerthree.net for our cloud tenant.  If you were in Mexico, Canada, or anywhere else outside of the US, you would only be able to connect to a non-US based DC.   
 
So, based on the end users longitude/latitude, it chooses Chicago as the closest.   There is also a configuration for a backup/secondary we call as well:  secondary.gateway.AmFam-US-Based-Only.zscalerthree.net if the initial one is not reachable.  But here's the item I'm pressing ZScaler on at the moment:
 
if the primary & secondary closest locations are in the same geographic city and therefore could (in theory) still use the exact same internet path to reach that city, is it smart enough to look elsewhere?   I suspect the answer is no.
 
My theory is the internet path to Chicago was having issues (from some ISP backhaul carrier coming from Missouri) whereas if say the primary was a Chicago DC and the secondary was say the Dallas DC (because you cannot have both the primary and secondary in the same city), it would have taken a different path and therefore would have recovered without any end user impact or involvement.

Fix notes:
Proposed fix notes from Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016949:

The issue was that Chicago has 2 datacenters for ZScaler and they were both the logistically closest primary and secondary locations (by geo-location) for users connected out of Missouri (Dallas was next closest).  In order to alleviate this issue, we would have to disable a data center for each of the cities with duplicate DC's.  That would currently be Chicago and New York City.  That would force the "secondary" to always take a different internet path to a different city than the primary.  This could have resolved this issue, but I would also note that if a regional ISP has issues that impact their internet routing, then "in theory" possibly could not reach either DC and you'd still have the same issues.  Currently assessing the possibility of doing this for Chicago due to the number of end users connected thru those DC's.  New York is far less of a concern with additional DC's available in Boston & Washington DC which are logistically very close to NYC.

From Zscaler Technical Support!
Your scenario makes sense, and you've identified a potential issue with geographical redundancy when both primary and secondary gateways are located in the same city. If there's a regional ISP issue affecting that city, it could indeed prevent traffic from reaching either gateway, causing a connection issue.

Understanding the Issue
Regional ISP Issues: If an end user's traffic cannot reach either the primary or secondary gateway due to an ISP issue affecting the entire region (e.g., Chicago), both gateways could become unreachable.
Geo-Location Based Selection: Zscaler's PAC file logic often uses geo-location to select the nearest gateways, which can lead to both primary and secondary being in the same city if multiple data centers (DCs) are available there.
Potential Solution
Diversify Gateway Locations:
Manual Selection in PAC: Instead of relying solely on geo-location, you can manually configure the PAC file to include gateways from different cities for redundancy.   This will not work for us as we have simplified our PAC's and use subclouds to control access.  I do have a potential mitigation thought but want to think more on it before proposing.  It is centered on only defining a single DC for Chicago and NYC (versus 2 for each) which would then force the secondary gateway thru a different geo-location.  Not "bullet proof" as it depends on the size/scope of an internet outage but would address this unique situation - more to come

09/05/2024 11:47:37 - rene.steele@amfam.com (Work notes)
Update from David B: a little background on the logic ZScaler uses to determine the data center to use.  There is no actual IP ping/probe but strictly uses the geo-ip location of the end users public IP (by longitude/latitude) and selects the closest DC location based on the ZScaler gateway defined in the local PAC file.  In our case, we limit users being within the US to only connect to US-Only DC's (mainly for source-ip application controls).  The every US based user goes to is:    gateway.AmFam-US-Based-Only.zscalerthree.net for our cloud tenant.  If you were in Mexico, Canada, or anywhere else outside of the US, you would only be able to connect to a non-US based DC.   
 
So, based on the end users longitude/latitude, it chooses Chicago as the closest.   There is also a configuration for a backup/secondary we call as well:  secondary.gateway.AmFam-US-Based-Only.zscalerthree.net if the initial one is not reachable.  But here's the item I'm pressing ZScaler on at the moment:
 
if the primary & secondary closest locations are in the same geographic city and therefore could (in theory) still use the exact same internet path to reach that city, is it smart enough to look elsewhere?   I suspect the answer is no.
 
My theory is the internet path to Chicago was having issues (from some ISP backhaul carrier coming from Missouri) whereas if say the primary was a Chicago DC and the secondary was say the Dallas DC (because you cannot have both the primary and secondary in the same city), it would have taken a different path and therefore would have recovered without any end user impact or involvement.

Problem statement: CFRHAB-9471: CFR 10 08 Not Attached to Renewal and Not Generating Letter
Description:
Description - CFR1008 not attached to renewal and hence not generating Pre Renewal Letters

Rootcause - 

TimeoutWF is responsible for triggering the "SendCyberPreRenewalLetterCFR1008" event, which generates the CFR1008 document. This workflow initiates on the 90th day and wakes up again on the 75th day to execute the event. If a renewal includes one of the below eleven replacement forms and the renewal status is set to "Renewing" the workflow will trigger the event.
 
('BPF8474-1023','BPF8475-1023','BPF8476-1023','BPF8477-1023','BPF8478-1023','BPF8479-1023','BPF8480-1023','BPF8481-1023','BPF8482-1023','BPF8483-1023','BPF8484-1023','BPF8485-1023','BPF8486-1023')
 
Although there are no direct conditions inferring the generation of CFR1008, the workflow will still trigger the event if any of the mentioned eleven replacement forms for CFR1008 are available.
 
There are two scenarios where the event will not be triggered:
1. If TimeoutWF does not initiate for a renewal. For example, if a renewal has any Pre-Renewal direction and remains in draft status, the workflow will not start.
2. If TimeoutWF reactivates on the 75th day, but the renewal has not yet entered the "Renewing" status. For instance, if the renewal remains in a quoted status due to a blocking issue.
 
For policy 910044894582, TimeoutWF initiated on the 90th day and reactivated on the 75th day; however, it could not generate the event as the renewal was not in the "Renewing" status.
 
Function addPreRenewalLetterEvent() in class AmFamCreateEventForEC.gs adds the event to renewal. And it is called by function startAlteredTermsNotice() in AmfamRenewalProcess.gs

Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016889

Cause Code:
vendor issue

Cause Notes:

Description

This issue consisted of two events

On 8/31 a change in the AWS S3 (Simple Storage Service) API provided by AWS caused failures in the

calls to that API from iGO and DocFast. The failure resulted in exceptions in previously working code and

prevented the documents from being written to S3. iPipeline resolved this issue through modifying the

calls to the AWS S3 API and deploying updated versions of iGO and DocFast.

9/4 – A rollback, by AWS, of the previous change was incompatible with the hotfixes applied by iPipeline

to resolve the 8/31 issue. After the rollback, metadata was not correctly applied, disrupting processing

of XML messages. This issue was resolved by reverting code, in iGO and DocFast, to the state that

existed prior to the 8/31 event.

This S3 API is used to support the upload of documents by users and for document transfer within

iPipeline systems and integrations.



Root Cause

IGo and DocFast leverage a supported mechanism in AWS S3 to post files to S3 with necessary metadata

tags to enable downstream processing. The API calls to S3 stopped working on August 31, 2024 due to a

change rolled out in the AWS infrastructure. As a result of this change, the API calls by iGO and DocFast

returned 400 errors instead of writing the files to S3.

Subsequently, on September 4, 2024, the API calls from iGO and DocFast to S3 failed a second time due

to a rollback in S3 of the changes previously made in the infrastructure. Due to the rollback, the new9/5/2024

mechanism for posting and tagging files was no longer supported and resulted in metadata necessary

for further processing not being applied correctly.

AWS provided iPipeline with the following statement regarding this issue.

“On August 30 2024, at 3:54 PM PDT, AWS deployed an update that, despite extensive testing,

inadvertently changed S3 API behavior for a small number of customers. Affected customers

who reached out to AWS Support were given guidance which, given this change, was correct.

Following the deployment, the service team identified that the update had caused the

unintended changes for the affected customers and on September 3 2024, at 4:23 PM, reverted

the change. The reversion that the service team performed was a standard response to

customer impact from a deployment. However, it resulted in a behavioral change that was in

conflict with the guidance from AWS Support after the initial deployment and resulted in

additional impact to customers who had followed the guidance.”

Problem statement: Slowness seen for the Native Mobile Services at TheGeneral
Description: We are seeing an unusual amount traffic and failed log ins on the mobile app at TG.
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016849

Cause Code:
Undetermined

Cause Notes:

There was a separate incident reporting MP web login issues. It was determined that CAS (login system) was having problems and it was restarted. After that, web worked fine. Mobile app also calls CAS, so it was double checked at that time. When looking at logins, it was noticed that there were A LOT of failures, all random email addresses. CPU of NativeMobileServiceV2 (mobile app backend) was fine, but that was likely was caused CAS to be overloaded and needing to be restarted. We are assuming that due to the amount of failures, there was some automation (malicious or not) that was being ran against the NativeMobileServiceV2 login endpoint. The high volume started at 2024-08-27 01:52:38.

The main issue in determining root cause is that we could not see where traffic was coming from. NativeMobileServiceV2 was not behind ThreatX and the client IPs were being NAT at the firewall so they were all the same on the app servers. We assume it was an attacker but don't have anything to point to for proof. If it does start up again, once NMS is behind ThreatX, then we'll be able to see where the traffic is coming from.

-Accounts are not being terminated properly

-de-provisioning workflow should terminate account(s) per IAM standards, comment, and move to the appropriate OU. 
-Accounts should be updated and synced with Azure to ensure exchange licenses are claimed.

-We have some mailboxes active on nonlicensed user accounts due to Entra account corruption, but we cannot clear the users as they are in a Synced OU.

software issue

Cause Notes:

Root Cause:
After troubleshooting data centers and network peripherals it was discovered a Windows updated was pushed by the customer to all laptops. Once this was discovered we rebooted the client and discovered this was the fix. 
 
Summary:
Corrinne reported that auto answer was not functioning. Upon engagement it was noticed that there were issues coming out of the data centers which lead us to believe the issue was on of the voice gateways. Testing this theory in the alternate data center showed it was resident in both data centers. 
 
Upon further investigation no errors were found which would cause this issue. Cisco TAC was engaged and engineers were troubleshooting. Upon troubleshooting, American Family had explained they did in fact put Windows patches on the laptops the prior night. 
 
Troubleshooting that route we had the users reboot their machine and the issue cleared up. It was determined that the Windows patch caused the Jabber client to lose some functionality (auto answer) while retaining the functionality to answer calls. All users were instructed to reboot their laptops at the end of the day. CDW implemented a change and reset all call center devices after hours through UCM as a precautionary measure as well.

software issue

Problem statement: CFRFARM-22317: FLR 00 09 - 01 22 cover letter is not inferring for MSA TX farm renewals
Description:
Description: As per the inference condition for this form (FLR 00 09 - 01 22), form should infer for MSA Texas FR renewals. But, the form is not inferring and failing at the EC end because of form is not present in the payload. Hence, Decs are not generating.

Root Cause: Availability of form is considering based on
1.If the specific state is configured in formpatternlookup table and 
2.PartnerID is not equal to null. 
But, for FLR 00 09 - 01 22 even though the state is matching, MSA Partner ID is not configured in the look up table. Hence, In renewal transactions, cover letter is not inferring.

Class Name: FormPatternEnhancement_AFI.gsx
FunctionName: isAvailable()#LineNumber:270

Replication Steps:
1.Initiate a Submission, fill all the required details.
2.Bind and issue the transaction.
3.Initiate a Renewal, fill all the required details and quote the transaction.
4.Navigate to forms screen, search for FLR 00 09 - 01 22.
5. Form will not infer.

Workaround:
1. IT team will suspend the message queue.
2. We will retrigger the declaration document via the backend, edit the payload, and add the missing cover letter.
3. Finally, we will resume the message queue and verify that the message is successfully processed.

From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016450

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

Premise:

Mapping for CLU and HAB industry code indicator have been wrong for quite a while. And our switch to use of integration view for payload generation exposed the issue (since we are now sending more info).
HAB was fine because the mapping for current and previous industry code were both wrong. Hence sapiens evaluator will never detect a change.
For CLU, only the previous indicator mapping was wrong. Hence the reason for the wrongly firing blocks.

Root cause: 
issue 1: At sapiens side, the industry code change is configured in for all lobs
issue 2: Due to recent middle layer changes this bind block is getting triggered for CLU polices.
Close notes: The resolution is a middle layer common flow mapping change to extract industry code from the payload coming from Fusion.

Problem statement: {I/S TECHDEBT} CA7 Job Failure - PR256002
Description:
The job PR256002 always has contention with P13CICS, each time the CICS team have been called out to address the contention, by manually closing the file PR02560Q. The job doesn't start executing until P13CICS gives up its allocation of the file. This happens when the file is manually closed.
so, to overcome this issue we need to change the position of the file in the job PR256002 from DISP= OLD to DISP=SHR.
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2017906

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

Job PR256002 has been entering a "WAIT" state due to the file AMFAMPV.PRO1102C.PR256000.PR02560Q being held by the CICS region on system MVS4. This wait occurs because the file is currently set with DISP=OLD, which causes the job to remain in a wait state. Job PR256002 waits for manual intervention to close the file.

Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016125

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

The applications in hscdmz.local that required the URL ssg.amfam.com was resolving to the External DNS IP address. When the change was implemented to resolve criblprod.amfam.com, this created a new DNS Conditional Forward zone in the hscdmz.local domain. This caused the URL ssg.amfam.com to now be routed to the internal IP.

The traffic was moved from originally ingressing into the AmFam DMZ since it is routed externally, to shift to SDWAN which is considered internal and was most likely being blocked by the Firewall rules.

Problem statement: CFRFARM-21450: Not able to remove a contact even though it was removed from all transactions.
Description:
Description: For farm ranch policies, a contact has been added under personal Liability Coverage as scheduled insured. when the user removed the contact from personal Liability Coverage, it is not removing in policy contacts.

Root Cause : When user tries to remove a contact from scheduled insured's under personal Liability Coverage in policy level Coverages screen. It is not removing the contact from backend.
 
Class Name:FRLineSchedCov_AFIEnhancement.gsx#removePolAddlInsuredScheduleItem#230
 
Replication steps: 
1.Initiate a FR Submission and Fill all the required details.
2.Navigate to Policy Coverage screen. Add scheduled Insured's under personal Liability Coverage in coverages's tab.
3.Navigate to Additional Insured's tab and we can now able to view all the scheduled Insured's added under personal Liability Coverage in coverages's tab.
4.Bind and Issue the transaction.
5.Initiate a new Policy change and Navigate to Additional Insured's tab and try to remove any contact which we added in previous transaction.
6.It will throw an exception stating that it needs to be removed from personal Liability Coverage.
7.Navigate to Coverage's tab and remove schedule insured under personal Liability Coverage. That will get removed under Additional Insured's in UI. But, not from backend.

workaround : Initiate a policy change, Navigate to Additional Insured's tab in Policy Level Coverages screen. Click on Add->Existing Additional Insured's and add the contact which we want to remove. select the contact and remove it. please refer below attachment on how to perform workaround.

Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016068

Cause Code:

From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016068

Cause Code:


Cause Notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2016061

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

  • After the OS patching operation, the project team performed a successful application sanity test.
  • It was discovered that upon initiating the V12 billing batch, it first picked up successfully but then became stuck.
  • To address this issue, the application was restarted twice during day, and the billing VM was restored. However, the situation remained unresolved.
  • The research revealed that the UAT environment had been refreshed recently with the PROD environment and the services was up on UAT environment.
  • Due to this, UAT environment created sessions with PROD database which results conflict with jbeam (V12 Billing Batch).
  • To fix this issue, all UAT services were turned down, a batch cleanup script was run on PROD, and only the ICD and Jbeam ports were restarted.
  • This resolved the batch's stuck issue, and the batch completed successfully.

Problem statement: Major Incident | Teams Extensions not reachable via AmFam 1-800 number
Description: When the AmFam 800 number is called and my extension is entered (31276) the system says that extension does not exist, however, when you call the Madison numbers (608-242-4100 or 608-249-2111) and enter my extension the calls get through. My extension is provided to the insurance departments in association with the AmFam 800 number. Is there a reason why my phone extension does not work?
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2015967

Cause Code:
software issue

Cause Notes:

At approximately 1am CST, the Genesys PureConnect Speech IVR 'RSNHQ1COPH01I3I' server initiated its normal timer-based API query to the PureConnect HelperService's ExtensionManagement.

At 1:23:39 am CST, the PureConnect HelperService queried the Radiant Logic LDAP backend (ldaps://vds.amfam.com:1636) for Skype user extensions. It used account I3IVDSS, search base 'ou=Corp_People,o=Pure_Connect' and filter '(&(objectcategory=person)(objectClass=user)(extensionattribute4= *))' and returned 16 results.

Log Snippet:
2024-06-11 01:23:39,255 [75] DEBUG PureConnectHelperService.ExtensionManagement.ExtensionManagementManager.QueryLDAPForExtensions[402] afe5f35c-fddf-486c-9593-ba27e0b4f31f - [!dt trace_id=5718f394036fd5bc1983724fbafdbdd8,span_id=bc3e31188d8c2122,trace_sampled=true] Records found for (&(objectcategory=person)(objectClass=user)(extensionattribute4= *)): 16 

PureConnect Helper service analyzed each of the 16 records and found only 2 with a valid 5-digit extension. This updated the ExtensionTable to match the LDAP query, as the source of truth for Skype users, removing the existing Skype user entries. 1800-MYAMFAM queries this database when asking people for a 5-digit extension, to check if an extension is valid to route. Users started noticing this morning with tickets to CallCenter and Voicemail, starting at 7:05CST.
Close notes: We have implemented a workaround to prevent the database from updating with partial information returned from LDAP, but the root cause for this fix is not from the Genesys end.

Problem statement: CFRHAB-9004: CU 21 11 Printing Duplicate Addresses / CU Having Duplicate Data
Description:
Description:  Impacts the CU 21 11 showing multiple address twice on CLU conversion renewal decs

Root Cause: In general, the form will display the Locations which are added under CU 21 11 exclusion along with that it will map the Locations of CLU underlying BOP policies. But for transition policies we identified the data present in the Database is not correct/Duplicate values. So, the payload is fetching that data and same is printing in the decs

We queried the database for last 6months and found few impacted transactions which are related to CLU conversion and having data issue
Eg:   C020150665, C020445851, C010996441, C020088635
 
Reported Production Transaction: C020445851/910039327058(CLU Conversion)

Workaround:  Data correction via script (SQL to remove/correct the location information- these locations are not being used on the policy).  

Steps to Replicate: (These are the steps to print decs, but to replicate the issue the transition Policy should have wrong data/Duplicate values in DB)

1)Create a CLU conversion renewal transaction
2) Add underlying BOP policies
3)In Policy Level Coverages, Add Locations under List of Scheduled Items (Premises) in CU 21 11
4)Quote and bound the transaction
5)Check the declarations


Further analysis required by conversion team.

06/11/2024 16:53:10 - Karuna Satish (Work notes)
Agents reported the following quotes: 88458181, 88455020, and 88454734, all of which have "System Error" listed as the DNQReason.

According to DD logs, the "System Error" occurred because the quest DNQ service failed with the error: "The request does not have minimum required fields. The arguments are stateCode= OH, FormCode = 9, UwCompany = 63, ReplacementCost = -1, PolicyEffectiveDate = Wed Jul 31 00:00:00 UTC 2024." The failure was due to the ReplacementCost being set to -1.

The ReplacementCost value of -1 was caused by a failure in the Service Broker Replacement Cost client, specifically "Xactware CalculateReplacementCost returned -1." Consequently, the Service Broker set the ReplacementCost to -1.

The Replacement Cost client failure, as noted in the DD logs, occurred because "IIS received the request; however, an internal error occurred during the processing of the request. The root cause of this error depends on which module handles the request and what was happening in the worker process when this error occurred. IIS was not able to access the web.config file for the website or application. This can happen if NTFS permissions are set incorrectly, or if IIS could not process the configuration for the website or application. The authenticated user does not have permission to use this DLL."

Attached are the logs for these errors.

Next step: We need the Infra team to further investigate the IIS error.

Problem statement: Common: Cancellation Information is not printing on the Termination Letter when it is Non-renewal transaction
Description:
Description: The cancellation Information is printing on the Sample document (Which is downloaded from Preview Under writer letter) and it doesn't print on the Actual UW termination letter.

Root cause: While fetching the information it is checking whether the renewal transaction is in non-renewing period or not.
If the Lead time is lesser than the current date, then it will not be moving to non-renewing status and does not printing any reason code and reason description in the termination letter.

The below condition "policyPeriod.UWCancellation_AFI.CancelReasons" is returning null if the renewal status is not Non renewing and failed to map details. 
If the status is non-renewing or Transaction type is Cancellation, then only the condition is satisfying.

Class: CancellationDetailsLetterDecorator.gs #52
PolicyPeriodEnhancement.gsx  #UWCancellation_AFI

Problem statement: We have identified an issue with claims in ECC that are closed and yet have Subrogation Status "open". Bug=CFS-2442
Description: We have identified an issue with claims in ECC that are closed and yet have Subrogation Status "open".  It appears users are able to close a claim while subrogation status is open or users are able to open/re-open subrogation status while claim status is closed. Attached is a report run identifying these claims.  There are several converted claims (ICS claim with 00, early 01 prefix claims, and Homesite, Connect and MSA claims with letter prefixes) that also have this status which was a decision during conversion, however, there are several more recent ECC 01-004 and 01-005 claims that demonstrate the described issue.
Cause notes:
System does not have limitations to prevent the subrogation status to be changed on a closed claim.  to prevent in future, we would have to add logic that would prevent this from happening and require the user to reopen the claim before they can change status of subrogation.

Discussed with subrogation manager and reporter of issue.  They will need to review list of claims and determine what direction they want to take.

Problem statement: Major Incident | Sales/PPC services seeing issues
Description: SQL upgrade made on 5/5, did not rebuild applications, new configs were not included in today's deploy.  Manually resetting, but we are several hours behind.
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2015759

Cause Code:
people process documentation

Cause Notes:

During the Homesite On-Prem Release on 5/23, some configs with old SQL instances / Port number values were put into Production. These were generated before the SQL Upgrade cutover project that switched instances / ports to new values, so they replaced the configs that had the new values. This was properly caught during the validation window, whereupon the Release team had to fix these affected config files manually.
Close notes:
To provide further details on the documentation update:
https://amfament.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RELENG/pages/16089317767/Config+Token+Changes

Specifically, this section has been updated and emphasized to be adopted as part of our prcoess:
"Update any existing builds currently in flight.  Since config files for all environments are generated as part of the build, you will need to identify any builds that have components that might not get rebuilt before they move to the next environment. For those identified builds, you will need to run a script to regenerate the existing configs using the new token values. For example, running "powershell.exe C:\RelEng\Scripts\Replace-ConfigItemValuesForBuild.ps1 -Version 132.0 -BuildEnv UAT -Platform 'Sales' -Component 'HSDLLs' -build 14" would regenerate the configs for that specific platform, version, build, component.  Make sure you do this step AFTER step 1 above as this script just regenerates configs based on current values. As an alternative to running the above script, you could obviously force out a build for each component and it will generate new configs using the values that were updated in step 1. The importance of this step needs to be called out because it has caused us issues in the past. It is best to regenerate the configs for ALL existing builds in all versions as opposed to just guessing which ones may or may not get deployed to other environments. We've had past issues where we selectively ran the regenerate script  only on builds and versions that we suspected would move to the higher environments only to find that a build we did not expect to move ended up getting deployed to prod. When this happened, it caused a major incident in production. Therefore, I'll repeat what I said above. It is best to regenerate the configs for ALL existing builds in all versions as opposed to just guessing which ones may or may not get deployed to other environments."

Close Notes:
To provide further details on the documentation update: https://amfament.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RELENG/pages/16089317767/Config+Token+Changes Specifically, this section has been updated and emphasized to be adopted as part of our prcoess: "Update any existing builds currently in flight. Since config files for all environments are generated as part of the build, you will need to identify any builds that have components that might not get rebuilt before they move to the next environment. For those identified builds, you will need to run a script to regenerate the existing configs using the new token values. For example, running "powershell.exe C:\RelEng\Scripts\Replace-ConfigItemValuesForBuild.ps1 -Version 132.0 -BuildEnv UAT -Platform 'Sales' -Component 'HSDLLs' -build 14" would regenerate the configs for that specific platform, version, build, component. Make sure you do this step AFTER step 1 above as this script just regenerates configs based on current values. As an alternative to running the above script, you could obviously force out a build for each component and it will generate new configs using the values that were updated in step 1. The importance of this step needs to be called out because it has caused us issues in the past. It is best to regenerate the configs for ALL existing builds in all versions as opposed to just guessing which ones may or may not get deployed to other environments. We've had past issues where we selectively ran the regenerate script only on builds and versions that we suspected would move to the higher environments only to find that a build we did not expect to move ended up getting deployed to prod. When this happened, it caused a major incident in production. Therefore, I'll repeat what I said above. It is best to regenerate the configs for ALL existing builds in all versions as opposed to just guessing which ones may or may not get deployed to other environments."

Problem statement: Users were unable to launch the VDI in Citrix workspace
Description: unable to launch VDI with the Citrix worksapce app
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2015712

Cause Code:
vendor issue

Cause Notes:

On May 17th, at 5:47:48 UTC (7:47:48 CDT) The Microsoft Azure Managed Service for AmFam Group VDI Experienced a sudden increase in demand for the Azure Compute SKUs we use, specifically VM sizes Es_V5 and Eas_V4. This spike resulted in capacity constraints. The impact of this constraint on AmFam Group was that 40-ish users of the AmFam Group were unable to connect to their VDI  as those VDI were not able to power on.

Attempts to use alternative SKUs (i.e. VM sizes) was unsuccessful as many other SKUs were also affected by the shortage of resources.

Below is the initial statement of the managed service outage. Note: it lists 10:47 UTC as when Amfam Group was identified as being impacted. We were aware of the impact well before this.

 

 

This is Microsoft's explanation of the outage:
Close notes:
Microsoft Azure is a Managed Service, and as such, we cannot "fix" their issue. This is the accepted consequence of using managed services. It should be noted this is the first recorded instance of the happening in the 4 years we have used Microsoft Azure.

We have the potential to mitigate the impacts of future resource shortages. Options include Microsfot Site Recovery Services, splitting users between East US and South Central regions, Using South Central US Azure as a business continuity site, etc.

However, these solutions involve increasing the monthly spend in Microsoft Azure, with the price increase depending on the solution selected. The costs range from "Moderate" to "Significant", depending on the approach.

As this is a managed service, there was no effective work around to Microsoft running out of computing resources.  As the outage progressed and the nature of its impact was understood, VDI resources from the New User Fulfillment pool was assigned to available users. However, by that time, Microsoft began to bring additional resources online and allowed us to power on the affected user's machines.

Problem statement: Users are unable to access the CCC Portal
Description: Unable to get into CCC portal.
Cause notes:
From Root Cause Analysis PTASK2015713

Cause Code:
environmental disaster

Cause Notes:

CCC vendor was facing performance issues. 

Complete RCA shared by CCC Vendor has been updated below.

"Thursday, May 16th , 2024, at 5:10 AM Central Time CCC began to experience an issue causing interruptions for CCC customers. The following services were impacted: CCC Portal, Total Loss Valuation, Assignment Routing (AAWS), Scheduling/Appointment Booking, CCC ONE Estimating, SSO - CCC Portal Home Page, SSO - CCC Portal Claim View, SSO - BRS Home Page and BRS Claim View, SSO-IES Home Page and IES Claim View, Return Data transaction processing, and processing of Casualty claims. We identified an extremely high load of failed requests and retries in our API Gateway (Google Apigee). This load impacted CCC systems listed above and caused high contention and resource stress on one of the main databases running in Amazon AWS. We engaged our API Gateway vendor, Google Apigee to assist with the issue. Thursday, May 16 At 7:13 AM Central Time, the database resources and entire cluster reached a critical state. A restart of the database cluster was initiated. At 9:41 AM Central Time CCC’s systems were restored. At 10:12 AM Central time, we continued to see higher than normal resource consumption at the database. At 10:40 AM Central Time, we took necessary preventive measures and disabled CCC ONE Estimating assignment and Estimate return data flow, this allowed other applications to function normally. At approximately 6:50 PM CT, assignment flow to CCC ONE Estimating was restored, and all CCC ONE units, upon connecting to the system, were able to download pending assignments. Our API Gateway vendor, Google Apigee, identified a bad version update which they applied May 14th . This combined with Google Cloud Platform backend performance issues in our API Gateway nodes were the root cause issue. A restart and redistribution of those Edge nodes was required to address the issue. Following this action, the high retry error rate decreased and returned to baseline.

Friday, May 17 At 4:00 AM we enabled the flow of CCC ONE Estimating return data. CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. At 7:10 AM Central Time, performance degraded impacting CCC applications. We disabled CCC ONE Estimating return data flow allowing CCC applications to recover. At 9:00 AM Central Time, CCC applications were restored and were functioning normally, the CCC ONE Estimating return data flow remained disabled. With our vendors, Oracle and Amazon AWS, we identified the root cause to be a malfunctioning automation at Amazon AWS. Following CCC’s restart Thursday, the AWS automation did not apply all database configurations at the Operation System and Kernel levels. CCC had no visibility to this configuration as it is a cloud-based service. At 11:00 PM Central Time, with AWS, we implemented the database configuration solution to resolve the performance issue.

Saturday, May 18 At 2:20 AM Central Time, we enabled all services and the system returned to normal performance.

Monday, May 20 – Tuesday, May 21 Monday, the system functioned as expected under very high load. Tuesday, at 5:10 PM Central Time, monitoring identified high internal database activity and performance degradation. CCC, along with AWS acted to mitigate the issue. We recycled the database nodes and services. This was completed by 6:32 PM Central Time and all services and system functionality was fully restored. The root cause of Tuesday’s interruption was the result of high load Monday and Tuesday causing internal database workload and node communication performance degradation to build up. We acted to control the load which reduced the delayed performance. Working with our vendor, RedHat, we have been provided additional optimization options at the data source level to assure that even with extreme load, we can provide the database backed communication the necessary capacity to recover. These changes are in testing."

Problem statement: CFRFARM-20553:  ERROR MESSAGE "Dwelling Cosmetic Hail Damage Coverage for Metal Roof or Siding" (KS state only)
Description:
Description: Receiving application error when trying to remove the coverage Dwelling Cosmetic Hail Damage Coverage for Metal Roof or Siding.

Root cause: The coverage has two questions and Cosmetic hail damage coverage applies to the metal siding surface on the dwelling and related private structures? is always setting the value to "TRUE" for Kansas State.

While removing the coverage it is throwing the null pointer exception, because for every toggle it is calling this function "setDwellCosmeticHailMetalSidingCovTermDefault" and when removing the coverage, it will return NULL for that coverage and causing Issue.

Class name: FRDwellingCoverageHelperAFI.gs
 setDwellCosmeticHailMetalSidingCovTermDefault#552

Impacted State: KANSAS

Workaround:  Remove the coverage with Script.

Replication Steps: 
1)Create Farm Ranch submission with Kansas state.
2) Add the same location and dwelling with the same state.
3)Select the coverage "Dwelling Cosmetic Hail Damage Coverage for Metal Roof or Siding" under dwelling additional coverages.
4) And now try to remove the same coverage it will throws the error.

ﾠ ﾠ1. The issue was introduced during performance optimization changes for archiving the data from PCT_INSTANCE_INDEX table.

ﾠ ﾠ2. The data form this table is also used by extract transaction to identify what all objects are available on a policy.

ﾠ 3. As the data was archived and moved to an archival table, respective changes were done in extract transaction to look for data in archival table as well and these changes were part of hotfix applied on Jan and Feb release.

Please note the date which was corrupted is just the reference cache data for a policy and not the actual transactional data. So, this should not have any impact on the actual transactional data of the policy.ﾠ

Preventive Measure -ﾠ

As a preventive measure we should make sure that the hotfixes are provided and installed until the issue fix is actually part of the Base policy release.ﾠ

For this issue we have the fix available as part of May release and till the may release gets install we should plan for installing the compatible hotfixes. In this case April release hotfix should be install after the environment gets upgraded with April release.

ﾠ 4. During spring release (March) the changes to look for archival table got overridden, Also the hotfix compatible for March release was missed out from base policy team which caused this issue to occur in first place.

ﾠ5. The hotfix on top of march release was provided by base policy team but by that time the data for some of the polices was already corrupted.ﾠ

6. We will be providing new hotfix to correct the corrupted data which will resolve the issue for corrupted policies as well

Diagnosis:

Identify the drop packets on traffic firewall logs and raised the firewall change CHG2122021 - RITM2641976 to allow the communication listed below :-

"dmx-corp-prod-1212" source zone on Rule no.735; AFI-SBC-to-MSA-SBC-For-Teams-Voice-sdwan on NHQ-Corp firewall.

Determine the Root Cause:

Communication between the MSA voice Session Border Controller (SBC) and the AmFam voice session border controllers, was requested on 10/03/2022 via RITM2290294.

Source Static IP MSA SBC 172.16.150.179 
Source NAT IP  MSA SBC      10.176.94.179
 
Destination IP NHQ 10.246.212.19 
Destination IP GRL 10.248.212.19 

Bidirectional RTP Port Range  30383-31382  
Bidirectional SIP Port UDP-5060

And Vice-Versa between source and destination

During the March 2022 timeframe, communication between AMFAM and MSA and vice versa is routed through the Transit zone via firewalls. The following path depicts the traffic flow without SDWAN.

On NHQ-Corp Firewall: dmz-corp-prod-1212 -> trust
On AFI-Tenant : AFI-WAN -> AFI-Transit
On MSA-Tenant: MSA-Transit -> MSA-WAN
On MSA-DC: MPLS -> dc-server-farm

  Vice-Versa

On MSA-DC: dc-server-farm -> MPLS
On MSA-Tenant: MSA-WAN -> MSA-Transit 
On AFI-Tenant : AFI-Transit  -> AFI-WAN 
On NHQ-Corp Firewall: trust  -> dmz-corp-prod-1212 

In August 2023, SDWAN was introduced for the MSA and AMFAM networks by ETS-ENS in partnered with Cyber Defense Border Technologies team. The traffic path between the AMFAM and MSA firewalls has been altered, with the transit zone firewalls removed from the path. During the process of updating the SDWAN rules on firewalls, it was not noticed to update zone "dmz-corp-prod-1212" on firewall security policy Rule no.735; AFI-SBC-to-MSA-SBC-For-Teams-Voice-sdwan and Rule no.774; MSA-SBC-to-AFI-SBC-For-Teams-Voice-sdwan on the NHQ-Corp firewall. 
Moreover, the connectivity between the MSA voice Session Border Controller (SBC) and the AmFam voice Session Border Controllers was never tested post SDWAN implementation. And the communication issue was reported on May 13, 2024 via INC3857198, and we implemented the firewall change CHG2122021 - RITM2641976 to allow the communication indicated below:-

"dmx-corp-prod-1212" source zone on Rule no.735; AFI-SBC-to-MSA-SBC-For-Teams-Voice-sdwan on NHQ-Corp firewall.

"dmx-corp-prod-1212" destination zone on Rule no.774; MSA-SBC-to-AFI-SBC-For-Teams-Voice-sdwan on NHQ-Corp firewall.
